articles.title: Week 8 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Jonah Coleman, Omar Cooper Jr. among top pickups
articles.summary: Justin Boone gives you his recommendations off the waiver wire at each position for fantasy football in Week 8.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

The Dolphins earned their first victory of the season on Sunday and Willis had his second straight quality fantasy performance — sandwiched around Miami's bye.

After finishing as the QB13 in Week 5, Willis was the QB4 overall this week. That result is thanks to a three-touchdown day (two passing, one rushing), as well as 208 yards through the air and another 37 on the ground. He's now run the ball at least eight times in three of his last four appearances.

The most exciting development for Willis has been the emergence of his skill position talent with Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington, Chris Bell, Greg Dulcich and Ollie Gordon II stepping up in recent weeks.

While the Patriots make for a tough test, Willis will have a much softer stretch versus the Lions, Colts, Bills and Jets again coming up after that. With his rushing upside giving him a solid fantasy floor, Willis will be a streaming option every week and now we're seeing the ceiling to go along with that in better matchups.

Kirk Cousins is 57% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add, if available.

Risky streaming options (if starter is out)

There's a reason why I haven't stopped highlighting Coleman in this column all season. In his first game back off injured reserve, the rookie immediately led the Broncos' backfield in what is now a three-man committee.

Coleman played nearly half the snaps, while RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins shared the other half. Coleman also led the team in scrimmage yards (69), touches (11) and routes run (11). Unfortunately, it was Harvey who scored a long touchdown and Dobbins who took a goal-line carry into the end zone.

Don't be misled by the final fantasy points though, Coleman's usage is what matters here. Sean Payton expressed a very clear desire after the game to get the fourth-rounder even more touches moving forward.

Though the ceiling might be partially limited at the moment with Harvey and Dobbins still involved, fantasy managers need to be aggressive anytime there is a potential starting back available on the waiver wire.

The Broncos have one of the five easiest fantasy schedules for RBs the rest of the way. Hopefully you took my advice and stashed Coleman, but even if you didn't there's still an opportunity to add him in 65% of leagues. I'm valuing Coleman as a possible low-end RB2 with upside.

Black is another rookie backup I've been featuring in this column all season, encouraging managers to stash him away in case of a Christian McCaffrey injury.

The veteran did get banged up on Sunday, but was fortunately able to return to the game in the second half. That led to increased usage for Black, who rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a score. It was his highest output since a 15-touch, 70-yard stat line in the opener.

McCaffrey downplayed the quad injury after the game and with a bye week to rest up, I'd expect him back at full health in Week 9. However, it's clear that Black is up to the challenge if his number is ever called.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last season isn't the worst idea in the world. Black should be rostered everywhere and would provide RB2 fantasy production with RB1 upside if McCaffrey ever missed time.

The trade rumors surrounding Jonathan Taylor seem like more than just speculation at this point. The Colts are also facing another very tough matchup against the division rival Jaguars in Week 8.

That might be why McGowan earned his biggest snap share of the season on Sunday (34.5%). It would be smart for Shane Steichen and company to get a look at what the seventh-round rookie can offer in a large role.

To McGowan's credit, he's performed well on his limited touches this year, including his season-high 48 yards against a stout Vikings' front in Week 7. With news of a Taylor trade potentially being announced at any moment between now and the Nov. 10 deadline, it's wise to stash McGowan on your bench until then. Let's just hope that Indy doesn't get a starting-caliber running back as part of the return in a JT trade. The Colts have one of the 10 best fantasy RB schedules in the second half of the season, so McGowan could be a sneaky fantasy option down the stretch and it won't cost you much to get him now.

Knight's value will evaporate the moment that Jeremiyah Love returns to the lineup. But if the rookie remains sidelined in Week 8, Knight will be an intriguing fantasy option against a generous Cowboys defense.

Over the last two weeks, Knight has been the more productive back in Arizona, racking up 161 scrimmage yards on 27 touches. Tyler Allgeier has only managed 97 yards on 30 touches. This will all come down to Love's availability, so don't go overboard trying to acquire Knight. He's just a spot starter if Love continues to sit out.

This is an extreme long shot, but Conner is a potential trade candidate who's sitting on IR in Arizona. I have the veteran stashed in several leagues, just in case the Cardinals send him to an RB-needy roster before the deadline.

Rachaad White is 55% rostered but would be the No. 2 RB add behind Coleman, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Mike Washington Jr. at NYJ (30% rostered)

Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. IND (24% rostered)

Cooper led this column last week and here we are again with him still barely coming in under the 50% rostered cutoff.

Even with Adonai Mitchell back in the lineup for Week 7, Cooper continued to shine with his second straight 100-yard outing. The rookie has now finished as a top-10 fantasy WR in back-to-back games with stat lines of 6-103-1 and 5-115-1. It also makes you wonder if he would have threatened the 100-yard mark in his debut, since he posted 30 yards on just five snaps before getting hurt.

After spending a month on IR, the first-round wideout looks like the real deal and has more favorable matchups on the way with the Raiders (Week 8), Bills (Week 10) and Dolphins again (Week 12). He was a must-add last week and now he's an "empty the waiver wire budget to get him" kind of pickup. Cooper is a high-end WR3 with a much bigger ceiling, which he has put on display the past two games.

Normally, I just list Tyson as a one-line sentence below, since he's rostered in almost 50% of leagues. However, his return is nearing and that rostered percentage isn't moving.

This is another talented first-round receiver who was dominating Saints' practices this summer before suffering another hamstring injury. It's hard to ignore almost everyone around the organization praising his skills and suggesting he would be a star at some point this season.

In Kellen Moore's fast-paced offense, there is plenty of room for another productive pass-catcher alongside Chris Olave… just ask Devaughn Vele.

It's not hyperbole to say that Tyson could be a major factor in fantasy leagues in the second half of the season when the Saints return from their Week 8 bye. You should have already stashed him in your IR spot, but if you didn't you can still solve that problem and get yourself a potential WR3 with WR2 upside once he's healthy.

With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks out of the lineup, Lemon had his best game yet with seven catches, 67 yards and a touchdown on eight targets against the Cowboys. We always knew Lemon was more of a long-term play, since he was a rookie who missed significant practice time in the summer due to injuries. So, it's great to see the first-round pick finally producing in what's been a chaotic season for the Eagles.

With speculation that Smith could miss more action due to his hamstring injury and no timeline on Wicks' return, Lemon is a must-add if he's still on the waiver wire in your league. He's a fantasy WR3/flex with the usual upside that comes with first-year players in the second-half of their debut campaign.

One of the most important things for first-year players to show in their early NFL action is that they belong on the field with the pros. While every player is different, when a rookie hits the ground running it's an obvious indicator of future success. When they're able to look comfortable and be productive, we have signals for stardom.

Douglas has managed to accomplish both those feats in his limited time on the field. After breaking onto the scene with a five-catch, 94-yard effort in Week 1, Douglas suffered an ankle injury that sidelined him for a month.

Coming off the bye, he picked up where he left off with 70 yards and a pair of touchdown catches.

While I'm not viewing Douglas in the same light as Cooper or Tyson, the third-rounder still has weekly WR3/flex potential and should be added in most leagues.

The Jaguars are returning from bye after a Week 6 outing where Hunter and Meyers were extremely productive.

Hunter only played nine offensive snaps, but was the first-read on many of those plays which led to four catches, 59 yards and a touchdown. With Brian Thomas Jr. getting fewer snaps and potentially going to be traded, Hunter's offensive involvement could rise. As we witnessed in his last game, it doesn't take much for Hunter to make an impact in real life and fantasy. Few players offer the kind of ceiling Hunter possesses, so he's an important stash.

Meanwhile, Meyers is a weekly WR3/flex option with double digit fantasy points in three of his six appearances this season. That includes a season-high 10 targets and 83 yards before the bye. Though I prefer chasing Hunter's ceiling, Meyers is the more proven fantasy option.

Terry McLaurin is done for the season, which opens the door for Williams to emerge as a consistent weapon in the Commanders offense.

The third-round rookie actually led Washington's receivers in snaps and routes run in the loss to the 49ers, finishing the game with 50 yards on three receptions. We've also seen him flash multiple times in the first six weeks, including a four-catch, 64-yard, one-touchdown debut and an 87-yard TD in Week 4 that was called back due to a penalty.

With all the attention on bigger names, Williams is sliding under the radar a bit as he returns from the Commanders' bye week. Make no mistake, Williams has WR3/flex potential with McLaurin out for the remainder of the season.

In deeper formats, you can also consider his teammate Treylon Burks, who stepped up in McLaurin's absence with four catches and 66 yards. He's also scored a pair of touchdowns this season. However, he walked off late in their last game with trainers, so we'll need to make sure he's healthy.

Brian Thomas Jr., Jaguars (trade candidate)

Thomas' rostered percentage has fallen far enough for me to include him in this column. This one is simple though, you stash him now and wait to see if he gets traded before the deadline.

A fresh start on a receiver-needy team could do wonders for the former first-rounder who put up 87 catches, 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2024. Doesn't that seem like a lifetime ago, considering how the last two seasons have unfolded for BTJ?

KC Concepcion is 60% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Cooper and Tyson, if available.

Tre Tucker is 58% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Cooper, Tyson, Concepcion, Douglas and Hunter, if available.

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

Terry McLaurin's injury also frees up more targets for Okonkwo, who is finally back to playing a normal snap share after missing time with a hamstring injury in the opening month.

Over his last two games before the bye, Okonkwo put up 60 yards on six targets versus the Giants and 69 yards on seven targets against the 49ers.

Prior to the arrival of Stefon Diggs, Okonkwo was one of my favorite sleepers this summer. With McLaurin sidelined, the 27-year-old tight end is once again set up to challenge for low-end fantasy TE1 value rest of season.

This isn't Strange's first appearance in this space, but he continues to be disrespected by fantasy managers. The 25-year-old is a high-end TE2 streamer with low-end TE1 potential.

Strange is averaging the sixth-most targets among tight ends over the last month and has at least seven targets in each of his outings during that span. He's also posted three very usable stat lines of 7-95-0, 7-68-0 and 5-44-0. That includes two top-12 weekly fantasy finishes.

While many non-elite tight ends have fantasy success due to touchdown-scoring, Strange is earning the kind of volume that could make his production more sustainable. Given his role in one of the best offenses in the league, Strange needs to be rostered, especially in a week with George Kittle and Isaiah Likely on bye.

Hunter Henry is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 TE add, if available.

T.J. Hockenson is 53% rostered but would be the No. 2 TE add behind Henry, if available.

Darnell Washington vs. CLE (3% rostered)

Cam Little is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 K add, if available.

Quarterbacks: Aaron Rodgers, Justin Herbert

Running Backs: Tyler Allgeier, MarShawn Lloyd, Kendre Miller

Wide Receivers: Xavier Worthy, Josh Downs, Chris Godwin Jr., Wan'Dale Robinson

Tyler Allgeier was expected to be the main beneficiary if first-round rookie Jeremiyah Love got hurt, but that's not how it has played out. Over the last two weeks with Love sidelined, Allgeier has split work with Bam Knight, with Knight being the more productive option. That led to Knight playing more snaps in Week 7. If Allgeier doesn't have one-injury away upside, then he doesn't need to be rostered.

When Josh Downs posted back-to-back 70-plus yard games in Week 2 and Week 3, it appeared he might have a chance to unlock a new ceiling the rest of the way with Alec Pierce sidelined. Unfortunately, he's failed to reach 50 yards in any game since and has settled into the low-ceiling flex territory for fantasy.

We all knew wideout Jordyn Tyson would eventually return and erase Juwan Johnson's fantasy upside, but Johnson didn't even wait for the rookie to get back in the lineup. The veteran has disappeared from the fantasy radar, while being limited to stat lines of 4-16-0, 0-0-0 and 1-7-0 the last three weeks. Now he's heading on bye and Tyson might be activated after that.

Mark Andrews hasn't topped 50 yards in a game this year and has been held under 30 yards in each of the past four weeks. The veteran is just a TD-or-bust fantasy TE2, who only has one score on the season.

articles.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 8: Latest news, updates on Lamar Jackson, Breece Hall, more players for fantasy football
articles.summary: We go over the Week 8 NFL injury report, sharing some fantasy football insights to help with your lineups.
articles.body:
This may be the cleanest the NFL injury report has looked all season. Or at least we didn't see many notable players go down with an ailment coming out of Week 7. Let's try not to jinx anything, though. It's tough enough on fantasy football managers already. So let's take a look at the Week 8 injury report and who we need to track for our fantasy lineups.

Jackson : This appears to be the only major QB injury we're tracking this week. Jackson has missed the past three games with a high-ankle sprain. We already have reports saying Lamar will play in Week 8 against the Bills on Sunday afternoon. Given how injury reporting has gone, let's see how Jackson's practice reports look this week. He could be limited a bit or hold a questionable tag going into the game. If Jackson is back, it's a boon for the entire Baltimore offense, particularly Derrick Henry, Ja'Kobi Lane and Mark Andrews. Zay Flowers has done fine for fantasy with Tyler Huntley under center, but has a better chance of consistently hitting his ceiling with Jackson at the helm.

Jadarian Price, SEA (chest) — Designated to return from IR

Hall : The Jets held Hall out for Sunday's loss to Miami and Braelon Allen ate up all the ground work again. The more Allen produces at a high level while Hall is out, the more likely he is to maintain a significant role in the offense upon Hall's return. That return appears likely to be Week 8 against the Raiders, though we'll monitor Hall at practice this week. If Hall remains out, Allen keeps his RB2 status and is one of the better fantasy backs again in a great matchup. If Hall returns, we'll need to see how the split shakes out, but he should be in your lineup. Allen should retain flex value with Hall back. We could see Allen command the early-down work while Hall takes snaps on passing downs.

Love : It's been a rough rookie campaign so far for the Cardinals' top pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. He's missed the past two games with a nagging ankle injury, but should have a shot to play in Week 8 against Dallas. Will he be a good fantasy play if he's active? That's far more uncertain than it looked in August, given how he's been used when healthy. Plus, Bam Knight has 128 yards on 22 carries (5.8 YPC) over the past two games with Love out. Knight has been better than Tyler Allgeier, so now we could see a three-back rotation once Love returns. That will make it difficult to trust any one RB until we see how things shake out snap/touch-wise.

Jones : The Vikings' back exited late in the win over Indy on Sunday and did not return. Jordan Mason was back in the fold, coming off injured reserve for Week 7. He led the rushing attack with 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones had eight carries for 26 yards and one catch. We know Jones' injury history, plus Mason looked better on his carries. We also know the passing game has been weak with Kyler Murray at the helm. If Jones sits, he reportedly avoided a serious knee injury , Mason is an RB2 given the type of volume he'd get. Even if Jones is OK for Week 8 against the Lions, Mason feels like the better option right now.

Waddle : It's been a rough go for Waddle in his first year in Denver, and a rough go for managers who invested a high draft pick in him. The wideout caught four of seven targets for 48 yards in Week 7's win over the Cardinals but was forced to exit with a chest injury and didn't return. He was trending toward another bust week and now is dealing with an injury. In shallow formats, Waddle could even become a drop candidate. Even if he plays in Week 8, it's a miserable matchup against the Kansas City secondary. If Waddle is out, it's tough to trust any other receivers in this passing game anyway. Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin would benefit but wouldn't be more than risky flex options.

Rice : The Seahawks' defense stifled the Chiefs on SNF in Week 7, one of the more dominating performances this season. Kansas City didn't get much going through the air as Patrick Mahomes had just 165 yards on 33 attempts with one INT. Xavier Worthy was out there the most with Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong and Cyrus Allen rotating in at WR. If Rice can return in Week 8, we would see the target tree condense, with Rice, Worthy, TE Travis Kelce and RB Kenneth Walker III getting most of the touches. Rice wasn't offering much upside prior to the injury, so he's merely a WR3/flex option. Worthy would be relegated to a risky flex against Denver.

Warren : The second-year TE missed his second straight game Sunday as the Colts fell to the Vikings. We didn't expect much from Daniel Jones against Minnesota's defense, but the passing game continues to be a negative. A road matchup against the Jaguars shouldn't get the pass game going either. If Warren comes back, it's tough to trust him as the TE1 we thought he'd be going into 2026. But he was posting decent numbers as Jones' preferred target, with 30 catches for 213 yards and two scores (one rushing TD) in five games. You can play Warren if he's active for Week 8, but temper expectations.

articles.title: Brewers’ historic rally blows away the Rays to move one win away from team’s first World Series title
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers used a historic fifth inning rally to blow away the Tampa Bay Rays, leading to a 10-1 in that moves them a win away from the title.
articles.body:
Milwaukee dominates, 10-1: The Brewers used a couple of soft hits to strike first, but then used a huge, eight-run fifth inning rally – all with two outs – to take a commanding lead. From there it was academic and the Brew Crew is up 3-0 in the 2026 Fall Classic.

World Series history: The Brewers’ fifth-inning rally set two new records in the Fall Classic. The seven consecutive two-out hits was a record, as was the eight-run burst the Brewers scored with two outs.

One win away: The Brewers last appeared in the World Series in 1982 and have never won a championship. They appear on track to rewrite franchise history – unless Tampa has a miracle comeback in store.

Tampa faces long odds: No team has ever come back from a 0-3 deficit in the World Series.

Our live coverage of Game 3 of the 2026 World Series has ended. Catch up with a full wrap of the action here and analysis from CNN Sports’ Hannah Keyser here .

There were nine innings of Monday’s Game 3, but it really all came down to one half-inning of history.

The Milwaukee Brewers used seven consecutive hits to score eight runs, all of which came with two outs, to trounce the Tampa Bay Rays and move within one win of claiming the franchise’s first World Series. Both those seven consecutive two-out hits and eight two-out runs were World Series records.

The Brewers got on the board first in the third with a couple of soft hits that found the right holes in the Rays’ defense. Jackson Chourio laced a single – his second in a day where he would go 4 for 5 – and Jake Bauers drew a walk. They cashed in when Christian Yelich hit his second bloop single of the game to bring Chourio in.

On the very next pitch, William Contreras dropped a single into right field where Victor Mesa, Jr. struggled to field it cleanly, allowing Bauers to score.

The Rays quickly went down in order repeatedly, dominated by Brewers’ starter Robert Gasser. When the Brewers came up in the top of the fifth, they were poised to make history.

With Chourio and Yelich having reached on a hit and walk, Contreras hit a chopper to third base, but replay showed Yelich beat the throw from a spinning Caminero at second, setting up a bases loaded situation. After a pitching change, Brice Turang then smashed a ball right back through the box and off the glove of Taylor Walls. Chourio and Yelich scored as the ball trickled into center field.

The Brewers kept the pressure on with a single from Garrett Mitchell and a double from Cooper Pratt to plate three more runs and suddenly the game was out of hand. Sal Frelick then hit a double into the left field corner to bring Pratt in for with yet another run.

After a pitching change, David Hamilton smacked a single into center field off Cole Sulser to score Frelick. Chourio, who is just 22, then came up and collected his second hit of the inning, a double to plate Hamilton from first base.

After that, things were pretty much academic (even if Frelick was diving in the outfield up 10 runs on his injured shoulder). The Rays scored once in the bottom of the ninth on Yandy Díaz’s long double to make it 10-1.

The Brewers look nailed on to win this series – and if they don’t, it’ll be a historic comeback for the Rays. No team has ever come back from 0-3 in the World Series to win the championship.

The first two games of the World Series were close – each ended with the tying run 90 feet from home on third base.

The crazy part is, they didn’t feel close. They felt like legitimate and legible depictions of how the Brewers never waver on the way to ultimate success. They felt like the Brewers were the better team.

But if there was any doubt, allow Game 3 to convince you.

The Rays – a great team, the other one-seed! – managed just three hits. They made outs on the basepaths again , and their regular season aggressiveness on the bases has started to look like a liability this series. Chandler Simpson made the catch of the postseason early on, but errors plagued them elsewhere.

What are you supposed to do against a team that can put up double-digits on small ball? The Brewers scored 10 runs without the ball leaving the park once. They scored eight of them with two outs in the fifth inning on a history-making seven-straight hits (no team has had that many consecutive hits in a postseason…ever).

The next time they came to the plate, they managed another couple singles that never came around to score, but the point is: These guys do not let up.

Jackson Chourio was 4-for-5. Robert Gasser – a 27-year-old rookie – faced the minimum through six innings. And the bullpen is usually the Brewers’ biggest strength!

It’s very probable the Brewers will win the World Series, possibly as soon as tomorrow night. It will be the first in the team’s history.

When they do, it will be because they undeniably deserve it. They have lost just one game this entire postseason. They swept the two-time champion Dodgers who are regularly and accurately compared to Goliath. They had the best regular-season record. They had the best regular-season record last year.

And, even if you’re uninterested in the labor implications, we should never stop marveling that a team which plays in the smallest media market in the sport, with a bottom-10 payroll, has established this level of consistent dominance.

Or, we’re about to witness an all-time comeback by the Rays.

Brandon Woodruff comes on in the ninth and immediately gets Victor Mesa, Jr. to fly out softly to right field. An infield single for Cedric Mullins followed and then Woodruff struck out Jorge Mateo.

Yandy Díaz stepped to the plate with two outs, just as he did in Game 2, but the stakes were levels lower this time around. With a full count, Díaz got the Rays on the board with a double to left-center field that he (and the Brewers outfielders) thought was gone. Mullins came around to score easily.

On the very next pitch, Jonathan Aranda grounded out to second base and it was all over.

The Brewers are one win away from the title!

Brandon Woodruff, who hasn’t pitched in a game since July 4, is in to pitch the ninth inning.

He is the longest-tenured Brewers player, and the erstwhile ace. But in recent years, he’s been plagued by injury. He hasn’t thrown more than 67 innings in a season since 2022.

The decision to put him on the World Series roster came down to the last minute, and it’s hard to imagine a more perfect opportunity to include him in this postseason run than this cushy final frame.

Brice Turang collected his third hit of the game with a double into the left field corner to lead of the top of the ninth inning.

Turang is one of four Brewers – along with Jackson Chourio, Christian Yelich and William Contreras – who have more hits than the entire Rays team.

Rays pitcher Steven Matz worked around the trouble though and sends Game 3 to the bottom of the ninth.

In a visceral manifestation of the Brewers’ relentless commitment to playing hard, Sal Frelick made a diving catch to keep the Rays at just one hit through eight innings.

It was a nifty play for the 2024 Gold Glove-winner. But even more than that, it was a stunning testament to how hard these Brewers play.

Frelick spent time on the injured list this year for a torn labrum that remains … well, torn. And probably pretty uncomfortable after hitting the artificial turf of the Trop.

Finally, Milwaukee appears to have taken their foot off the gas, seemingly content to coast to victory and a commanding 3-0 lead in the World Series.

No team has ever rallied from 3-0 down to win in the Fall Classic. In fact, no team has even managed for force a Game 6 in the World Series after going down three game to none.

The Rays have six more outs until they’re facing that scenario.

The goal for the Brewers now is to get their most trusted, and oft-relied upon, relievers an extra day of rest by keeping them out of the game.

The goal for the Rays should be to force Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy to dip into his circle of trust.

The Rays are failing at that goal now, too, along with the “winning a baseball game” goal. Gasser is gone, but the Rays are still retired in order in the seventh.

Garrett Cleavinger came on to pitch the seventh inning for the Rays, and proceeded to sit the Brewers down in order.

Even more impressively, Cleavinger managed to strike out Brewers’ lead-off man Jackson Chourio, who had been 4-for-4 in the game to that point.

Barring a historic comeback, the Brewers are poised to push the Rays to the brink of elimination.

The Rays lead off the sixth with a walk from Victor Mesa, Jr.

Then Nick Fortes grounds into a double play, Taylor Walls grounds out, and somehow Robert Gasser has still faced the minimum in this lopsided clinic being put on by the Brewers.

Gasser is first Brewers pitcher to get even a single out in the sixth inning this whole postseason, and he completes the frame easily.

The Brewers started the 6th inning with 13 hits to the Rays’ one, and Milwaukee went looking for more.

William Contreras and Brice Turang got back-to-back infield hits and the Brewers once again had ducks on the pond.

Cole Sulser managed to escape the inning unscathed, but the Brewers are putting on a textbook example of their “small-ball” style that has confounded opponents all season.

Remarkably, the Brewers have put up a 10-spot through six innings without the benefit of a home run.

It is highly unlikely that the Rays will come back in this game. And they definitely will not come back in this game if they continue to go down in order.

Ironically, Tampa still has the three hardest-hit balls of the game – including Yandy Díaz’s 115.5 mph single, which is the hardest hit ball of the postseason.

New pitcher, same result for the Brewers – and we’ve got history in the World Series.

David Hamilton smacked a single into center field off Cole Sulser to score Sal Frelick.

Jackson Chourio, who is just 22, then came up and collected his second hit of the inning, a double to plate Hamilton from first base. Next, Jake Bauers mercifully hit a flyout to end the inning.

But the damage was done – seven consecutive two-out hits from the Brewers to put this game out of reach, a World Series record.

Milwaukee’s eight runs in the inning are two more than the Rays have scored so far in the entire series. It’s also a World Series record for most runs in an inning scored by a team with two outs.

Rays third baseman Junior Caminero made a nice leaping catch to rob David Hamilton of a hit to start the fifth inning.

It was a good thing, too, because Jackson Chourio came up next and collected his third hit of the game.

Jake Bauers hit a flyout, then Christian Yelich worked Freddy Peralta for a walk, and the Brewers suddenly had a chance to break the game wide open.

The Brewers’ postseason hero William Contreras was up next and hit a chopper to third base, but Yelich beat the throw from a spinning Caminero at second, setting up a bases loaded situation.

That was the end of the line for Freddy Peralta, who was replaced by Cam Booser to face Brice Turang.

Turang then smashed a ball right back through the box and off the glove of Taylor Walls. Chourio and Yelich scored as the ball trickled into center field.

The Brewers kept the pressure on with a single from Garrett Mitchell and a double from Cooper Pratt to plate three more runs and suddenly this game is out of hand.

Sal Frelick then hit a double into the left field corner to bring Pratt in with yet another run.

Six two-out runs have crossed for the Brewers in the inning, and they’re still batting as the Rays make another pitching change.

At the end of this series, the final party will begin. It will be the last in a long line of them.

Every major US sport has multi-round postseason schedules, but none of them party like MLB teams. Locker room celebrations in the NFL tend to be subdued until the Super Bowl, and since hockey players are famously superstitious, popping bottles early is practically verboten in the NHL; the Stanley Cup is all that really matters.

Boston Red Sox clubhouse manager Tom McLaughlin has spent over 40 years with the Red Sox, and he says he’s lost track of how many celebrations he’s been involved in, but he counts them in the dozens. He told CNN Sports it was “pretty tame” when he started in the ‘80s, when the postseason was much shorter, but the back end of the season now can feel like one enormous bender for the most successful teams.

Successfully navigate the wildcard round? Let’s get wild.

Made it through the Divisional Round? Get another round in.

Won the Championship Series? We’re going on a spree.

By the time a baseball club wins the World Series , let’s just say that the celebration will not be their first rodeo. Everyone will have had plenty of practice.

William Contreras had the most challenges among catchers in the regular season and he flexes that propensity again to help Robert Gasser complete another 1-2-3 inning.

While we’re at it, the Brewers have been calling Contreras “Bill.” That’s all I’ve got to make this post interesting. Rays, help me out!

Freddy Peralta performed a rare feat in the 4th inning – he retired the Brewers in order.

Peralta struck out Garrett Mitchell and Cooper Pratt, which injected some much-needed life into the crowd in St. Pete.

A groundout from Sal Frelick ended the inning in quick fashion, but the Rays need to find a way to break up the rhythm of Brewers’ starter Robert Gasser and do it quickly.

Through three the Rays are making solid contact off Robert Gasser – two of the outs in that frame were over 100 mph off the bat – but he’s managed to face the minimum and given up just a single hit, back in the first.

In a word: he’s cruising, with credit to the Brewers defense, which has been airtight so far tonight.

Another inning, another rally for the Brewers.

After a quick out, Jackson Chourio laced another single – his second of the game already – and Jake Bauers drew a walk, and Freddy Peralta was right back in the soup.

This time, they cashed in as Christian Yelich hit his second bloop single of the game to bring Chourio in for the first run of the game.

Peralta escaped the inning without any further damage, but the Rays once again find themselves in the unenviable position of playing catch-up against the Brewers.

articles.title: Valencia CF: ¿Por qué vale 1.250 millones un club que factura poco más de 100 millones?
articles.standfirst: La entrada de Pitchwise Holdings como nuevo socio de Peter Lim en el club, y con una inyección inmediata de 100 millones de euros en caja
articles.summary: La entrada de Pitchwise Holdings como nuevo socio de Peter Lim en el club, y con una inyección inmediata de 100 millones de euros en caja
articles.body: El Valencia CF abre una nueva etapa de su centenaria historia. Peter Lim, que controla el club desde hace 12 años a través de Meriton, ha encontrado nuevos socios para llevar al club a su siguiente etapa: Pitchwise Holdings. Un next level que arranca con una valoración de 1.250 millones de euros del Valencia CF. Descontados los gigantes Real Madrid y FC Barcelona, que además son clubes sociales, sólo el Atlético de Madrid superaría al club che en valor. ¿Cómo ha llegado el club a esta cifra? La valoración anunciada por el club de LaLiga rompe muchos de los esquemas actuales de tasación, y denota una fuerte confianza en el crecimiento del negocio a largo plazo. Habitualmente, la industria del fútbol se mueve en unos múltiplos que oscilan entre dos y seis veces los ingresos ordinarios a la hora de establecer cuánto vale un equipo de fútbol. En el caso del Valencia CF, ese multiplicador más que se dobla respecto al rango alto de los clubes considerados premium, al situarse en casi doce veces su cifra de negocio. LaLiga Stock Market 2026, el informe de valoraciones que elabora anualmente 2Playbook, situó al Valencia CF en el noveno puesto del ranking, con un valor de mercado actual de 370,5 millones de euros. En ella no se suman las expectativas de Pitchwise y Meriton sobre el potencial de revalorización de sus activos inmobiliarios, el negocio del nuevo estadio y otros crecimientos futuros. De inicio, el fondo estadounidense entra en el accionariado con una inyección de 100 millones de euros que, inmediatamente, reforzarán la caja valencianista. El grupo estadounidense se hará con una participación del 42% entre la compra de acciones y la ampliación de capital, mientras que Lim mantendrá por ahora la mayoría accionarial. En la valoración del club se incluyen un buen número de activos, pero hay dos que son claves para entender la cifra final: Mestalla y el Nou Mestalla. El valor de los terrenos donde se sitúa el actual estadio y el potencial negocio que se contempla para el futuro recinto, que se contempla como una palanca del crecimiento del club con una oferta mayor y negocios a pleno rendimiento los 365 días del año. Además, cabe recordar que Valencia es la tercera ciudad más poblada de España y la masa social valencianista una de las más fieles y numerosas del fútbol nacional. Todo ello metido en la coctelera permite comprender algo mejor las claves de la segunda mayor operación corporativa del fútbol español en lo que va de 2026. Peter Lim llegó al Valencia CF en 2014, en un momento de fuertes dificultades financieras para el club. La Fundación Valencia CF, principal accionista, necesitaba resolver su deuda con Bankia y el club buscaba un propietario que garantizara su continuidad. El empresario singapurense desembolsó 94 millones de euros por el 70,06% de las acciones, en una operación que incluyó 22 millones en efectivo y otros 72 millones financiados por Bankia. La adquisición se articuló junto a una refinanciación de la deuda del club, que rondaba los 230 millones de euros y debía devolverse en un plazo de 15 años. El plan de entonces se centraba en una fuerte apuesta por elevar los ingresos y el rendimiento deportivo (se acometieron fichajes de renombre los primeros años), con el objetivo de recuperar la presencia habitual del Valencia en Europa y completar el nuevo estadio. La realidad, en el cómputo general, ha sido distinta: la entidad ha atravesado años de pérdidas, ha reducido su inversión en plantilla y ha permanecido alejada de las competiciones continentales. El proyecto del Nou Mestalla, además, quedó paralizado durante años. Eso sí, se garantizó la supervivencia a largo plazo del club. La propiedad ha tenido que aportar recursos adicionales para sostener al club en esta década, con capitalizaciones que superan los 160 millones de euros en total. A los 100 millones de euros de la ampliación de capital realizada en 2015 se sumaron distintas operaciones de financiación y capitalización de préstamos. En 2021, Lim convirtió 43,3 millones de euros de créditos vencidos en capital. Un año después, prestó otros 35 millones de euros, de los que 17,6 millones se capitalizaron para compensar las pérdidas soportadas estos años. Este verano, Meriton dio luz verde para capitalizar otros 35 millones durante 2026-2027, si bien esta operación no ha sido aún inscrita. ¿La razón? La estructura de la operación corporativa anunciada el pasado viernes se divide en dos tramos: compra de acciones directamente a Meriton -no se ha desvelado a qué precio- y una aportación adicional al club de 100 millones de euros por parte de Pitchwise a través de un préstamo convertible en acciones. La misma fórmula seguida por Lim todos estos años. Sea como fuere, permitirá al Valencia elevar su límite salarial por si necesitara acudir al mercado de fichajes en enero, entre otros aspectos. Entre la compra de acciones, ampliaciones, préstamos y conversiones, Meriton Holdings ha invertido cerca de 300 millones de euros en el Valencia CF en estos doce años al frente, según datos extraídos de Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. La deuda es otra de las claves de la operación, y del camino del Valencia CF a partir de los 2000. Si nos ceñimos a la era Lim, el club continúa soportando un volumen de deuda relevante, pero la fotografía es muy diferente. Cuando llegó el empresario singapurense, la deuda era a corto plazo y las urgencias mucho mayores. Ahora esta deuda está más ordenada y con un calendario de vencimientos más amplio. La financiación original, ligada a Bankia –y posteriormente asumida por CaixaBank–, se ha reestructurado y sustituido por nuevas operaciones ligadas al Plan Impulso de CVC y LaLiga, así como a la construcción del Nou Mestalla. Igual que hiciera el FC Barcelona con el Spotify Camp Nou, el Valencia apostó por Goldman Sachs para la financiación de su estadio. Con la gestora de fondos firmó una refinanciación de 186 millones de euros en otoño de 2024; ésta consta de una línea de crédito a largo plazo de 121 millones y un préstamo puente de 65 millones. Con ella, el club canceló sus deudas corporativas financieras anteriores y liberó garantías, incluida la hipoteca sobre el actual Mestalla. Adiós a las deudas con CaixaBank, Gedesco y Rights & Media. El segundo gran movimiento llegó en junio de 2025, cuando la entidad aseguró 322 millones de euros para terminar el nuevo estadio. El paquete combinó una emisión de bonos de 237 millones, con un plazo de devolución de hasta 28 años y un interés fijo del 5,82%, y un crédito de 85 millones a cinco años. Este último se planteó para ser amortizado con los ingresos de la venta del suelo del actual Mestalla. A 30 de junio de 2025, la deuda con entidades de crédito ascendía a 121,7 millones de euros, incluidos los intereses devengados pendientes de pago. A ello se sumaban 152,3 millones de euros en otros pasivos financieros, de los que 65,1 millones correspondían a la deuda con el fondo de titulización del Nou Mestalla. Al tratarse de partidas contables distintas, no deben interpretarse como una única deuda bancaria homogénea. Pero el cambio más relevante se ha producido en la estructura de vencimientos. El club ha trasladado una parte sustancial de sus obligaciones a plazos más largos y ha vinculado parte de la financiación a los futuros ingresos del nuevo estadio. La operación de 2025 mejoró el capital circulante hasta los 160,2 millones de euros positivos, frente a los 94,3 millones negativos del ejercicio anterior. Sin embargo, el fondo de maniobra seguía siendo negativo en 19,8 millones. La previsión del club pasa por cambiarlo a positivo cuando el nuevo estadio esté a pleno rendimiento. Los nuevos inversores han basado parte de sus perspectivas en el potencial de negocio del club con el cambio de casa, especialmente tras una década de cierta estabilización de su facturación. El Valencia CF que se encontró Lim en 2014 facturaba 81,1 millones de euros de cifra de negocio (sin contar traspasos de futbolistas). En 2024-2025, la cifra alcanzó los 103,7 millones, lo que supone una tasa de crecimiento de apenas el 2,5% interanual en todo el periodo. En LaLiga EA Sports, eso sí, no es sencillo superar los 100 millones de ingresos ordinarios sin competir en Europa. Por líneas de negocio, la televisión continúa siendo una fuente clave, aunque la ausencia de competiciones europeas y los resultados deportivos han limitado su crecimiento. El área comercial, por su parte, ha recuperado capacidad y ya genera alrededor de 24 millones de euros por temporada. En el negocio de día de partido, los abonos y las entradas aportaron 26,4 millones de euros en 2024-2025. La mejora, sea como fuere, resulta limitada para una afición exigente con un club que se sitúa en el top-6 del fútbol español, representa a la tercera ciudad del país en población (840.792 habitantes) y cuenta con una base social fiel: 40.000 abonados, cifra que se va a 47.000 entre socios y abonados. Ahora, con el Nou Mestalla y sus 70.000 asientos, se prevé un fuerte incremento en la partida de abonados, ticketing y VIP. Una cuestión que no es menor, pues el matchday se ha convertido en una de las partidas más diferenciadoras a la hora de medir el equilibrio competitivo de la competición. También es un punto clave para mantener sólidos los beneficios que ha venido generando el Valencia estas dos últimas temporadas (falta conocerse el cierre de 2025-2026). En la vuelta a beneficios ha sido clave el plan de ajustes de la masa salarial y contención del gasto de la entidad desde la pandemia. En el cómputo general, la era Lim se ha saldado, por ahora, con unos números rojos acumulados de 187,8 millones de euros. En 2025-2026, el Valencia fue el sexto club de LaLiga EA Sports por asistencia media, con 44.601 espectadores por partido y una tasa de ocupación del 90%. El dato refuerza el atractivo de una entidad que, incluso en temporadas alejadas de la zona alta, mantiene una demanda elevada en Mestalla. La marca Valencia CF también conserva atractivo para atraer a patrocinadores nacionales e internacionales. Puma es uno de sus principales socios y el proveedor técnico de referencia del club, mientras TM Grupo Inmobiliario figura en el frontal de la camiseta. Con la marca deportiva, de la que es su principal club en LaLiga, tiene garantizado un contrato hasta 2029, y con la inmobiliaria valenciana, hasta 2028. Asimismo, el club trabaja desde hace años en un plan de crecimiento de su negocio retail y de merchandising con colecciones exclusivas y líneas de moda, la apertura de nuevas tiendas propias y el refuerzo de su ecommerce. La cantera es el tercer activo diferencial. La VCF Academy ha seguido abasteciendo de talento al primer equipo cuando las finanzas no permitían tantos fichajes y la venta de algunos de estos jugadores de la casa ha generado altos beneficios en esta última década. Cristhian Mosquera, traspasado al Arsenal FC en el verano de 2025 por 15 millones, es el último ejemplo. Hace pocas semanas, el club firmó a Braulio Vázquez como nuevo director deportivo, una apuesta por un hombre de larga trayectoria y éxito en CA Osasuna, y que debe reforzar esta parcela clave para el presente y futuro che. Sea como fuere, el Nou Mestalla es el principal argumento patrimonial de la valoración. Las obras comenzaron en 2007 y quedaron paralizadas en 2009, después de que el proyecto inicial se volviera financieramente inviable. Durante años, el esqueleto del estadio se convirtió en una gran losa para el crecimiento del club. La solución ha requerido modificar el proyecto y conseguir nuevas licencias, además de asegurar la financiación. El presupuesto final alcanza los 400 millones de euros y, si nada se tuerce, el Valencia podrá estrenar su nueva casa en 2027. Penner Sports Group aporta el gran know-how en la parte inversores del deporte. El grupo familiar de Greg y Carrie Penner tiene participación en los Denver Broncos de la NFL y en los Colorado Rockies de la MLB. Greg Penner es, además, presidente del consejo de administración de Walmart y socio fundador de Madrone Capital Partners. La presencia de los cofundadores de KKR añade, por su parte, capacidad financiera y experiencia en inversión a largo plazo, aunque no significa que KKR, como firma, pase directamente a controlar el Valencia. El fondo está muy involucrado en los festivales de música y el sector del entretenimiento, otra clave del crecimiento del negocio del fútbol. ¿Qué le puede ofrecer el Valencia a este holding? En primer lugar, el acelerón en la parte inmobiliaria y patrimonial rebaja el riesgo de la inversión. Y, por otro lado, los 100 millones aportados de inicio deberían espolear a la dirección deportiva para intentar crecer en el césped. articles.title: Kylian Mbappe loses Chinese sponsors for calling Mao ‘Chinese dictator’
articles.summary: Mbappe appears to say that the funniest internet meme he’d seen was of his face imposed on that of ‘a Chinese dictator’.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe has been dropped by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football superstar apparently joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

“Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement on Tuesday, adding that “with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe”.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid forward, who until this incident was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media.

Mbappe is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme.

“With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe,” Mengniu said in a statement.

“Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people,” it added.

The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face digitally altered onto that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures.

“Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo.

One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks … crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable.”

Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their energy drink bottles.

Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people” and “have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people”.

In September, Mbappe addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator in an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe.

“There’s a part of it that’s funny. You can tell that, for some people, it’s all in good fun. But there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said.

“Being compared to individuals who murder others, or who have brought misery to millions upon millions of people – well, I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life,” he said.

The furore in China came a day after Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d’Or, the most prestigious individual award in football.

Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there.

Former NBA player Dwight Howard referred to Taiwan as a country in 2023 as he appeared in a video with the island’s vice president and current President William Lai Ching-te, causing fury on Chinese social media.

Beijing claims Taiwan is its territory and has threatened to use force to take control.

Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey posted a tweet in 2019 supporting Hong Kong protests, leading to China suspending sponsorship deals with the NBA and pulling games off Chinese television for a year.

articles.title: 'Deep Brew' arrasa a Tampa Bay y acaricia las Series Mundiales
articles.standfirst: Los Brewers funcionan como una computadora, hacen un partido casi perfecto y ganan 1-10 a los Rays para otear el primer anillo de su historia en la MLB
articles.summary: Los Brewers funcionan como una computadora, hacen un partido casi perfecto y ganan 1-10 a los Rays para otear el primer anillo de su historia en la MLB
articles.body: Los Brewers, el equipo del año en la MLB, continuaron con el ejercicio de demolición al que han sometido a sus rivales en los playoffs. En el tercer partido de las Series Mundiales, Milwaukee arrasó a los Rays 1-10 y se puso 3-0 en la final con cuatro partidos por disputarse. El equipo que dirige Pat Murphy está a un triunfo de conseguir el primer título de su historia. St. Petersburgo, donde juegan los Rays en el estado de Florida, fue un paraíso tropical para los Cerveceros, inabordables. Sólo permitieron un hit en seis entradas para continuar con el trabajo de desmoralización con el que primero destruyeron a los imbatibles Dodgers (4-0) en la final de la Liga Nacional. Los Brewers se han convertido en una máquina perfecta de jugar al béisbol. Ya les llaman 'Deep Brew', en honor a Deep Blue, la computadora que en 1996 desafió en Philadelphia a Gary Kasparov, el campeón del mundo de ajedrez. Todos los abridores de los Brewers llegaron a base, ocho de los nueve impulsaron una carrera, y Jackson Chourio conectó cuatro hits —a uno de igualar el récord de la Serie Mundial en un solo partido— al final de la quinta entrada. Es difícil jugar mejor. Para un equipo que llevaba 44 años sin jugar unas Series Mundiales, la respuesta al reto es formidable. Anotaron ocho carreras con dos outs en la quinta entrada. Una jugada histórica. Los Brewers, fundados en 1969, no sólo pueden ganar el primer título de su historia y dejar en cuatro el club de las franquicias que nunca han conquistado el anillo: Rays, que están 'jugando' estas Series Mundiales, San Diego Padres, Colorado Rockies y Seattle Mariners. Milwaukee puede igualar la gesta de los Reds de 1976, la Gran Máquina Roja como los llamaron, que han sido los únicos en ganar una Serie de Campeonato y las Series Mundiales sin perder un partido. El título parece asegurado. Nunca se remontó un 0-3 en unas Series Mundiales.

articles.title: Carlos Linares: un accidente de moto por salvar a un perro, un oro mundial y el primer billete a Los Ángeles 2028
articles.standfirst: El jienense tiene una carrera meteórica en tiro: debutó a nivel nacional en 2021 y cinco años después se ha proclamado campeón del mundo
articles.summary: El jienense tiene una carrera meteórica en tiro: debutó a nivel nacional en 2021 y cinco años después se ha proclamado campeón del mundo
articles.body: Carlos Linares todavía no ha terminado de asimilarlo. Es el primer español en lograr la plaza para los Juegos Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028 gracias a su oro en la prueba P4 de pistola a 50 metros SH1 en su primera participación en un Mundial. "Todavía no me lo creo, nunca he participado en unos Juegos. Me hace mucha ilusión, pero no quiero pensarlo porque aún porque queda mucho", reconoce riendo al otro lado del teléfono. El jienense no llegaba a Changwon (Corea del Sur) en su mejor momento anímico. La Copa del Mundo de Serbia, disputada en julio, le había dejado tocado. "En el deporte hay valles y estaba un poco decaído. Mi intención en Corea era ver si mentalmente había trabajado lo suficiente", explica. Su clasificación no hacía presagiar el oro. Terminó séptimo, con 535 puntos. Los ocho primeros accedían a la final. Antes de empezar a disparar, le dijo a Manuel Sáez, su entrenador: "Hace un buen día para ganar un oro". A partir de ahí, fue otro. Concentración absoluta y ejecución perfecta. En el quinto tiro de los 24 se puso primero y ya no soltó ese puesto hasta el final. "Fue increíble, la final soñada", reconoce. Changwon, además, para él es talismán. El año pasado consiguió allí su primer oro en una Copa del Mundo. Al escuchar entonces el himno no pudo evitar las lágrimas. "Estaba sintiendo lo que siente Rafa Nadal o la selección de fútbol y es por mí", pensaba en el podio. Para entender el camino hasta Corea del Sur hay que retroceder al 1 de mayo de 2007. Linares tenía 25 años y su vida giraba alrededor del trabajo, las motos, los viajes y los amigos, como cualquier joven de esa edad. Trabajaba como carrocero de camiones, fabricando grúas de asistencia en carretera, y el deporte no ocupaba un lugar importante en su día a día, aunque lo practicaba desde que tenía uso de razón, sobre todo el baloncesto ya que mide 1,91 cm. Aquel día salió de ruta con un grupo de motoristas desde Jaén hacia la sierra de Cazorla. Era una salida normal, hasta que, al salir de una curva y llegar a una recta, vio un cachorro sentado en medio de la carretera. En el intento de evitar atropellarlo, la moto cayó por un desnivel de unos tres metros. Él salió propulsado, el vehículo golpeó su espalda y le provocó una lesión medular. "Demasiado que no me maté", recuerda. Su familia ya había sufrido dos pérdidas traumáticas: un tío falleció en 2002 en un accidente con un camión y otro murió en 2004 también en la carretera. Su accidente, en 2007, supuso un nuevo golpe. "El accidente me hizo madurar. Cambié el chip", explica. Pasó nueve meses en el Hospital Nacional de Parapléjicos de Toledo. A partir de entonces tuvo que reconstruir su vida. "A partir del accidente lo he probado todo para saber dónde estaba mi sitio", confiesa. Siempre había jugado al baloncesto y regresó a Jaén con la intención de formar un equipo de baloncesto en silla de ruedas. No fue posible. Después probó el pádel, pero él no entiende el deporte sin competir y tampoco había posibilidades ahí. Descubrió el tiro casi por casualidad. En una gala en la que premiaron su labor en una asociación que trataba de acercar el deporte adaptado a Jaén conoció a Miguel Navío, que le invitó a participar en una jornada de puertas abiertas en una galería de tiro en diciembre de 2019. Allí probó la carabina y le gustó. Desde el principio le dijeron que tenía un don, que era un diamante en bruto. Pero la pandemia interrumpió aquella primera aproximación, pero después regresó a los entrenamientos y se compró una pistola. En 2021, en su primera competición nacional, la Copa del Rey de aire comprimido, logró un récord de España. Un año después debutó a nivel internacional. Le preguntamos por el secreto de su meteórica carrera. Él no duda al responder: "Mi punto fuerte es la técnica porque mi primer entrenador era un subteniente de la Guardia Civil y me inculcó la disciplina a rajatabla, la técnica y el trabajo". Porque el tiro en silla de ruedas no tiene adaptaciones. Los blancos mantienen las mismas dimensiones y la distancia de tiro no cambia, pero el deportista compite desde una posición más baja y debe controlar la estabilidad sin agarrarse a la silla. No hay cinturones que lo sujeten, como ocurre en otras disciplinas como el baloncesto en silla o el tenis. El oro mundial no ha cambiado su rutina. Linares entrena en el pabellón Manuel Jara Labella, donde se encuentra la galería de aire comprimido, y realiza las sesiones con armas de fuego en el Club de Tiro de Precisión Jaén. Alterna las tres modalidades que practica con sesiones de gimnasio tres veces por semana y trabajo psicológico. Sólo en tiro acumula entre 20 y 22 horas semanales. Las medallas, de momento, permanecen guardadas en una caja, siguiendo el consejo de Juan Antonio Saavedra, triple medallista en Juegos. "Al final te envenena", resume. Ahora le espera un 2027 cargado de competiciones, con pruebas previstas en Francia, Australia, Estados Unidos, Serbia, Suiza, Croacia y Emiratos Árabes. Un calendario exigente para seguir creciendo antes de afrontar el gran desafío de su carrera: Los Ángeles 2028. "De momento sólo quiero disfrutarlos y hacerlo lo mejor que pueda. Si consigo medalla, estupendo, pero no está dentro de mis objetivos", dice.

articles.title: Harry Kane’s forgotten childhood moment with Katie Goodland resurfaces as the couple celebrates football’s biggest honour
articles.summary: Harry Kane’s greatest footballing achievement has given fans another reason to look back at where his journey began.
articles.body: Harry Kane’s greatest footballing achievement has given fans another reason to look back at where his journey began. The England captain won the 2026 Ballon d’Or on Monday, October 26, ending a 25-year wait for an English winner. Yet, amid the celebrations, an old photograph from 2005 has captured hearts online. It shows a young Kane standing beside David Beckham, with a girl who would eventually become his wife, Katie Goodland. Nearly 21 years later, their shared history has turned the image into a reminder that some of life’s most meaningful moments begin long before anyone knows what lies ahead.Harry Kane and Katie Goodland’s childhood photo with David Beckham goes viralThe photograph dates back to 2005, when Beckham opened his football academy in Greenwich, London. Kane, then a schoolboy with dreams of making it in professional football, attended the event alongside other young players from his school.At the time, the picture offered a glimpse of a young football enthusiast meeting one of England’s biggest sporting icons. Few could have predicted that Kane would go on to captain his country and become one of the most prolific strikers of his generation.Even fewer would have imagined the personal story unfolding beside him. Goodland, who attended the same school as Kane, was among the children at the event. She would later become his wife and the mother of their children.The timing has made the photograph particularly special. What once looked like an ordinary childhood memory now connects Kane’s early ambitions with the life he has built away from the pitch.Transfer News Live highlighted the remarkable coincidence in a post on X, writing:“In 2005, Harry Kane posed for a photo with David Beckham alongside a girl from his football academy.Since then, he has married her, they've had children together, supported each other through everything and shared an unforgettable moment last night as Harry won the Ballon d'Or. 😍Nothing but respect. 👏❤️”Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or win makes the moment even more specialKane’s success on Monday gave the old photograph a fresh meaning. The Bayern Munich striker claimed the 2026 Ballon d’Or after scoring 73 goals for club and country during the 2025-26 season. He finished ahead of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to secure football’s most prestigious individual honour.The victory also ended England’s long wait for another men’s winner. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to claim the award, back in 2001.For Kane, the achievement reflects years of persistence, steady improvement and an exceptional season in Germany. For fans, however, the childhood photograph offers something beyond statistics and trophies.It captures the journey from an aspiring young player to a global football star, with a familiar face beside him throughout the years.His Ballon d’Or triumph may mark the highest point of his career so far, but the resurfaced image reminds supporters that success is often more meaningful when shared with the people who were there from the beginning.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
