articles.title: Trade Ideas for Dylan Larkin and the 10 NHL Teams on His Approved List Amid Rumors
articles.summary: Slowly but surely, the NHL's unfinished business from the offseason is starting to get taken care of.
articles.body:
Slowly but surely, the NHL's unfinished business from the offseason is starting to get taken care of.

Forward Kirill Marchenko was moved from the Columbus Blue Jackets to the Toronto Maple Leafs just before the start of the season, while the Blue Jackets finally ended their tough negotiations with top center Adam Fantilli.

The Anaheim Ducks managed to get all of their restricted free agents signed.

Goalie Connor Hellebuyck has a new home, going from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils this past week.

Restricted free agent defenseman Alexander Nikishin re-signed on a one-year deal with the Carolina Hurricanes.

Now we just need the Detroit Red Wings to get all of their business done, ranging from a new full-time general manager to a contract for restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson to the trade request that is still lingering out there for center Dylan Larkin.

When it comes to the Larkin situation, he is currently playing for the Red Wings, but a trade still seems inevitable at some point this season. Maybe it finally happens when they get a full-time general manager. Maybe interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has the freedom to make a trade and pull something off sooner rather than later.

Either way, we still do not know when any of that will be, or which exact team it will involve. We might, however, be able to start narrowing it down now that Larkin has reportedly increased his approved trade list to 10 different teams.

So let's take that list and try to come up with a trade idea that might work with each of them.

Or at least the type of offer each of them could make.

Some will be easier than others given the assets each team has (or does not have).

There is also the question of whether or not those teams actually need (or want) Larkin, and if the Red Wings have any interest in what they have to offer. Some of these are just bad matches for both teams. But whether they need him or not, and whether or not Detroit wants what they have, we are still going to come up with some ideas.

We are simply going through the list alphabetically, and not based on who is more likely to get him.

It is easy to see why Larkin would want to play in Carolina.

After spending a decade playing on losing hockey teams, he would be joining one of the league's steadiest contenders and the defending Stanley Cup champions.

Carolina also makes a lot of sense from a practical perspective because it is loaded with first-round draft capital, has a really good farm system, and has the salary cap flexibility to take on Larkin's contract.

The problem: There is not really a short-term need for Carolina to be heavily in the market for Larkin.

The Hurricanes already go three-deep at center with Sebastian Aho, Logan Stankoven and Jordan Staal, with all three signed through at least next season. Maybe Staal, who is getting closer to the end of his career, takes on a smaller role down the lineup, but adding Larkin would seem to be more of a luxury for Carolina than a necessity.

But since they are on the list, let's put together an idea.

The idea: Carolina trades center Jesperi Kotkaniemi, two first-round picks, and forward prospect Bradley Nadeau.

Kotkaniemi is more of a salary-dump/throw-in to create a roster spot and clear some additional salary cap space in Carolina. He's still only 26 years old and can at least give them an NHL-caliber depth center, and maybe there's a path for him to contribute.

Carolina's farm system isn't overly deep at center when it comes to potential impact players, so maybe Detroit wants to take a talented winger instead. After all, even if the Red Wings are losing a center in the trade, they still need more talented help all over the lineup. The first-round picks would not be early picks (Carolina has all three of its picks over the next three years and a future Dallas pick), but they could at least be potential future trade assets.

It's a good match for Larkin. There are some assets here that could help Detroit long-term. But it's not a perfect fit from a Carolina needs perspective.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Low, but not impossible. Carolina could make it work from a lineup standpoint, and it does have some assets, but it might not be the right assets or the best match for Carolina.

As long as Colorado plays Nazem Kadri on the wing, there could be a need for another center here behind Nathan MacKinnon and Brock Nelson.

Adding a player like Larkin into that mix would be as imposing a top-three center grouping as there is in the NHL.

But how do the Avalanche make this work?

Their farm system is one of the worst in the NHL.

They have no first-round picks over the next two years.

There are some decent young players on the roster, but nobody who really projects as an impact player.

It's just not a great match for Detroit.

But, because they are on the list, we are going to try and come up with something.

So what could Colorado potentially offer? There's not much.

The idea: Colorado trades C Gavin Brindley, C Fedor Svechkov, and a 2029 first-round pick for Dylan Larkin.

This is why Colorado is an unlikely match. Actually, it's why Colorado is a terrible match for Detroit. Brindley and Svechkov are two decent young players, but neither is a prime prospect or somebody who is going to meaningfully move the needle. The next first-round pick Colorado has is in 2029, and it's hard to imagine the Avalanche moving a veteran player, or having one that Detroit is going to have a use for.

Colorado would need to get a third team involved somehow, and even then, it just doesn't seem likely.

Larkin might approve a move there, but it seems like a low-percentage chance given the assets.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Almost non-existent. Just not enough trade assets.

The Stars are still very much in their Stanley Cup contention window, and Larkin would be a really good piece to have down the middle with Roope Hintz and Wyatt Johnston.

There is also probably some added incentive to go all in this season, given the long-term uncertainty around winger Jason Robertson and his expiring contract after this season.

But do they have enough to offer for Larkin?

That depends on how bold everybody wants to get.

From a prospect and young center perspective? Probably not.

The idea: Dallas trades D Thomas Harley and a 2027 first-round pick to Detroit for Dylan Larkin

We know Dallas is willing to move Harley because they attempted to do so this offseason for Zach Werenski. Granted, that would have brought back another top-tier defenseman, and moving Harley for Larkin would leave a hole at the top of their blue line, but moving out Harley's contract would make the money and salary-cap situation work from a Dallas perspective.

Even though Detroit has a bigger need at center, Harley could help give them an outstanding top-four with Moritz Seider and, ideally, Simon Edvinsson if they can get him signed and convince him to stay long-term.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Slim. Dallas could use him, but its best trade asset (Harley) would leave a big hole on its defense that it would have to find a way to eventually fill this season.

If Aleksander Barkov's injury were of the season-ending variety again, it might have opened the door more for Florida.

But given that he will be back at some point, and after they gutted their long-term trade assets to put together a package for Brady Tkachuk this offseason, it would be really hard to make something work here.

The only offer that makes sense from a Detroit perspective is probably one that Florida would laugh at.

The idea: Florida trades C Anton Lundell and LW Sandis Vilmanis for Dylan Larkin.

Lundell is younger and cheaper than Larkin, and even though his offense has not really taken off, he remains an essential cog in their machine and is an outstanding defensive presence. Detroit would almost certainly have interest in him, but it might not be appetizing for Florida to make that move.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Very low. Not enough prospect depth or draft pick capital to entice the Red Wings.

As far as logical spots go, there isn't a better one than this.

The Wild need another impact center to play behind (or in front of) Joel Eriksson Ek.

There are Team USA connections all over the place with Matt Boldy, Brock Faber, and Quinn Hughes on the roster, while Bill Guerin is the general manager.

Minnesota is in win-now mode and, like Dallas, probably has some added incentive to push all of its chips into the center of the table given the potential departure of Hughes after this season.

The Wild are almost certainly interested, and they absolutely should be.

The idea: Minnesota trades C Danila Yurov, G Filip Gustavsson and a first-round pick to Detroit for Dylan Larkin

The Wild gutted a lot of their farm system and young NHL talent a year ago to get Hughes out of Vancouver, but there are still some pieces here to move.

They have all of their future first-round picks, while Yurov is a talented young player who has the ability to play center or wing while possessing a lot of untapped offensive potential.

But what about Gustavsson? Minnesota has Jesper Wallstedt as its long-term starter, and given the contract he is set to get, it probably doesn't make a ton of financial sense to have two goalies making more than $6.8 million per year on the roster (and Wallstedt will certainly make more than that). That could (and maybe should) make Gustavsson a potential trade chip either this season or in the offseason.

Detroit has no goalie signed beyond this season, and while it does have some intriguing prospects at the position, goalie prospects might be the most unreliable and unpredictable asset in the league.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: High. It just makes too much sense. They just have to find the right pieces.

Despite a lack of success in recent years, the Devils obviously believe they have a chance to win, and to win very soon. If they did not believe that, they would not have traded for starting goalie Connor Hellebuyck.

The Devils already have one of the league's better 1-2 center duos with Jack Hughes and Nico Hischier, and adding Larkin into that mix as the No. 3 guy would go a long way toward elevating this team to an immediate contender.

If championship teams are built down the middle, there are not many better teams down the middle than Hughes, Hischier, Larkin and Hellebuyck would be.

That lineup would become even more imposing next season if the Devils were able to add Quinn Hughes alongside his brothers, Jack and Luke.

New Jersey has four first-round picks over the next three years, including two in 2027, but is there enough beyond that to get Detroit's attention, especially after trading Dawson Mercer and Alexander Command for Hellebuyck?

And can New Jersey make the cap work? It is pretty much capped out this season and already has over $96 million committed for next year. That could easily go up if it lands the third Hughes brother.

The idea: Devils trade F Arseny Gritsyuk, D prospect Anton Silayev, two first-round picks

It's more futures-based, but Gritsyuk is a talented player who is off to a really good start, while Silayev is arguably one of the best prospects still remaining in the Devils system. If you're an all-in team, or think you might be, those prospects and picks are more valuable to you as trade chips. Might as well use them.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Higher than it might have seemed at the start of the season. Definitely a team to watch, but do they have enough left to trade?

Even as their core group of players gets older, and even as the playoff success has dried up in recent years, you always know Tampa Bay is going to be a contender and in the mix for any top player that becomes available.

They always find a way, and they are not afraid to deal draft picks.

While the Lightning do have two really good centers in Brayden Point and Anthony Cirelli, Larkin would be a very strong addition and give the lineup a little bit of a spark that it might need. They also have a couple of young center prospects that could be NHL players and could get Detroit's attention.

The idea: Tampa Bay trades C Conor Geekie and two first-round picks for Dylan Larkin.

Geekie is still unproven, but he is working his way into the NHL lineup and has great size and talent that could make him a second-line player. While future first-round picks from a contender might not be intriguing, Detroit might want to play the long game here.

The Lightning still have their 2028 and 2029 first-round picks, and a core that is starting to reach its limit for contention.

Nikita Kucherov is 33 and not signed beyond this season.

How good are these guys still going to be, and how good of a core are they still going to be, two years down the line? Maybe that 2029 first-round pick has some sneaky good value. Maybe Tampa Bay starts to transition to a new chapter at that point. None of these teams have first-round picks that are likely to produce a star-level player, but one of those future Lightning picks might actually be a sneaky good opportunity to get something.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Medium, but probably closer to low. Even if it might be a good chance at serious long-term value, the Red Wings might not be interested in waiting that long for a payoff from a Larkin trade.

Of the teams on Larkin's reported list, Minnesota has the biggest need for him.

But Utah might have the best trade assets that should get Detroit's attention.

Two of Utah's best prospects are centers (Tij Iginla and Caleb Desnoyers) who project to be potential top-six players.

They have four first-round picks over the next three years.

And they are a team that is starting to enter a win-now mode where they might be willing to dip into that prospect and draft pick pool to get immediate help.

Utah already made a big trade this offseason for a center, acquiring Vincent Trocheck from the New York Rangers, and they do already have Logan Cooley (who can play center or wing) and Barrett Hayton as options down the middle.

Nick Schmaltz can also move between center and wing.

But Larkin is better than Hayton, and adding him could allow Trocheck to slide into more of a matchup/defensive/penalty killing role and open up the other forwards on the team to focus more on offense.

The idea: Utah trades C prospect Tij Iginla and two first-round picks to Detroit for Larkin

The two teams already have a recent history of making deals after Utah sent a first-round pick to the Red Wings for goalie Sebastian Cossa, and Utah definitely has the type of players Detroit would be looking for in dealing Larkin.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Reasonably high. It's a good match for what everybody is looking for here. Utah gets a top-six center for a contending team. Detroit can get a high-upside young center. There is something here that could work.

Like Tampa Bay, Vegas is one of those teams that, no matter the salary cap outlook and no matter how thin its prospect pool is, will find a way to get the player it wants.

The Golden Knights have done it repeatedly over the years, so you can never really count them out.

It's also not a surprise that Larkin would have Vegas on his list given how players want to play there for a variety of reasons.

But this might finally be a situation where Vegas has met its match in piecing together an acceptable offer.

The idea: Vegas trades F Braeden Bowman, F prospect Jakob Ihs-Wozniak, and two first-round picks.

Maybe you can get Vegas to part with Trevor Connelly, but that might be a big ask given his start to the season. Any offer Vegas puts together is likely to be more of a quantity-over-quality package, and that's just not going to entice Detroit.

Chances of Larkin being traded here: Low. Just a bad match for Detroit.

Among the teams that have tried to thread the needle between rebuilding and contending, the Capitals seem to have pulled it off better than most. Even though the early-season results are not quite there, this team still has all the makings of a contender.

They also have more trade assets than most of the teams on this list, including some potential NHL options that could help Detroit right now.

The idea: Washington trades C Ilya Protas, F prospect Ivan Miroshnichenko, and a first-round pick for Dylan Larkin.

Would the Capitals be willing to split up the Protas brothers? Maybe not, especially given Ilya's high upside. But Larkin would be an immediate upgrade for a team that should have its sights set on contending this season and perhaps beyond.

Dylan Strome and Pierre-Luc Dubois are occupying the top-two center spots right now, but Strome is unsigned beyond this season, and Dubois has run into some major injury concerns over the past two years.

Miroshnichenko has been outstanding in the AHL, but has not yet stuck in the NHL and has been given permission to seek a trade.

You could swap Aliaksei Protas in for his brother, even though he is a winger, and it would be a very comparable package to what the Capitals sent to the St. Louis Blues this offseason for Jordan Kyrou. While Aliaksei is the more proven and established player, Ilya is a better positional fit for what Detroit might be looking for in a Larkin trade.

Chances Larkin gets traded here: Medium. I could see it. The Capitals are in a weird spot where they should have a chance to win, but they don't really have a lot of truly high-end players. They also have some good trade assets. The biggest problem might be the reality that Washington has a bigger need for defensive help right now and might need to use its trade assets to fix that.

articles.title: A Tiffany Stratton Swerve Loading, Champion Sami Zayn is Thriving, More WWE Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The Save Mart Center in Fresno, California hosted the October 26 episode of Raw on Netflix where the women's division took center stage.
articles.body:
The Save Mart Center in Fresno, California, hosted the October 26 episode of WWE Raw on Netflix where the women's division took center stage.

Liv Morgan learned she would defend the Women's World Championship against Becky Lynch and needed The Judgment Day to save her from The Man and a Tiffany Stratton cash-in attempt.

Sami Zayn made a surprise appearance and retained the Undisputed WWE Championship against Je'Von Evans thanks to Bron Breakker, with Penta looming as a potential cash-in threat.

These events and more highlighted a show with major fallout on the road to Crown Jewel.

Since winning the Money in the Bank briefcases, both Penta and Tiffany Stratton have teased cash-ins multiple times. Raw was especially egregious with both looking ready to cash in on the same night.

These failed fake-outs do nothing but make the Money in the Bank holders look bad. This has been especially true for Stratton.

On SmackDown and Raw, WWE contrived situations where Liv Morgan only remained champion because Tiffy forgot what she was doing until The Judgment Day pulled the champion to safety.

Fake-outs like this hurt Austin Theory's credibility after his MITB win in 2022, and his eventual failed cash-in only compounded the problem.

Penta should not be cashing in any time soon, so fake-outs only make it look like he is failing in his plans repeatedly.

At least Stratton does look like she will be successfully cashing in soon, but WWE needs to write situations that are better timed to make everyone look competent.

Tiffany Stratton's Cash-In Teases Point to a Chelsea Green Swerve

Tiffany Stratton is repeatedly teasing cashing in against Liv Morgan, who has slipped through her grip time and again.

The most forgettable outcome would be for Tiffy to finally catch Liv and walk away with the gold, but that is not the most likely scenario.

Instead, the teases have set the stage for a swerve: Stratton cashing in on Chelsea Green.

It would be especially heartbreaking if Green managed to beat Morgan for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship, only to immediately lose her world title.

This makes more sense for everyone involved and lets Tiffy lean into a more natural heel role by turning on her own friend.

Sami Zayn Deserves Lengthy Run as Undisputed WWE Champion

Sami Zayn showed his value as undisputed WWE champion once again, giving Raw a strong leading voice in the men's division while Roman Reigns took the week off.

His opening promo and match against Je'Von Evans delivered, adding necessary weight to a show that was otherwise understaffed.

As a test of how far Zayn can go, this segment was a rousing success that made clear the fresh heel can carry the gold for a while.

The best outcome would be for The Last Real Good Guy's antics to keep him strong until WrestleMania 43 where someone can step up to finally humble him.

In the meantime, there is no reason to hot-shot the title anymore. Cody Rhodes and CM Punk have had their time at the top, and there is plenty of time to sell Kevin Owens chasing Zayn before he wins big.

Penta's Makeshift Team with Je'Von Evans Is a Detour from the World Title

After just two tag matches together, Penta and Je'Von Evans have earned themselves a World Tag Team Championships match at Crown Jewel on Nov. 7.

While this makes sense after Mr. Money in the Bank and The Young OG defeated Bron Breakker and Austin Theory in non-title action, it is not an interesting angle.

Penta has the Money in the Bank briefcase and should be in the world title conversation. A tag team diversion does little to strengthen his world title credentials.

If Penta is going to be stuck in a tag title program, he could at least team with his brother, Rey Fénix. The two could be great tag champions.

Penta and Evans are not the type of team that elevates a struggling tag team division, especially when it is obvious WWE is just delaying the inevitable with Penta.

Evans would benefit more from joining forces with an established tag team against The Vision, as Seth Rollins did with The Street Profits earlier in the year.

Nathan Frazer and Axiom are doing almost nothing on SmackDown, work a similar style to The Young OG and deserve a tag title run more than a makeshift duo.

Lyra Valkyria and Bayley Exit Lengthy Feud with No Direction

Lyra Valkyria and Bayley finished up their feud with a strong match that did not feel as definitive as it should have.

The main problem was WWE's failure to capitalize on Valkyria's strong start to the feud. She came out of the first match dominant, only to do nothing. Even a second win over Bayley when she returned led nowhere.

By the time the bell rang, only the result of this final battle mattered, and Bayley defeated Valkyria by submission.

Since WWE has shown little interest in pushing The Role Model or The Valkyrie, it is hard to say what was even accomplished over the course of this feud.

Other wrestlers have treated their feud as a nuisance in backstage segments. Bayley's victory also carried limited weight, given Valkyria's struggles against other opponents in recent months.

Bayley is unlikely to get into the Women's Intercontinental Championship scene seriously, and Valkyria as a lone heel without credibility may be in need of another character reset already.

articles.title: Ranking Penta's 5 Best Ways to Cash In WWE Money in the Bank Contract
articles.summary: Penta is Mr. Money in the Bank, and all eyes are on the luchador for when he might choose to cash in his world title opportunity.
articles.body:
Penta is Mr. Money in the Bank, and all eyes are on the luchador for when he might choose to cash in his world title opportunity.

Assuming WWE never again wants to have the briefcase cashed in on a midcard title like the United States Championship, he has one of two titles in his view: the WWE Championship or World Heavyweight Championship.

Currently, those titles are held by Sami Zayn and Roman Reigns. Both are intriguing options, but the path to the gold has many branching paths.

How should Penta cash in his briefcase? When should he call his shot? Where would be the most exciting place for the cash-in? Keep reading for the best options to make Penta's moment truly special.

5. Penta Rushes to Gold, Dethroning Sami Zayn on the October 30 SmackDown

Pro: Penta wins the gold in shocking fashion and sets himself up for a rematch with Roman Reigns as well.

Con: This would not allow Penta to keep running with his unique briefcase and might lead to him losing the title quickly.

On the October 23 SmackDown, Penta teamed with Trick Williams and his own brother, Rey Fénix, to defeat Sami Zayn, Johnny Gargano and Ricky Saints.

The end of SmackDown teased that Zayn will defend the Undisputed WWE Championship against Trick on Friday's show.

This could set up Penta to dethrone Zayn after the champion cheats to retain against Williams.

The positive with this idea is that Penta could get a rematch against Reigns at Crown Jewel after this win, allowing him to even avenge that loss at a major premium live event.

However, another defeat to The OTC could undercut Penta's momentum. Separately, CM Punk and Kevin Owens would remain threats to his WWE Championship reign.

Either man is more likely to go to WrestleMania 43 with the Undisputed WWE Championship, which would mean that Penta's title reign would be shorter than he deserves.

4. Penta Cashes in on Sami Zayn After His Men's Crown Jewel Championship Match

Pro: Gives Penta a big title win on a memorable stage and sets up the luchador to be the focal point of SmackDown through the rest of 2026.

Con: Again, Penta has a great briefcase to carry around and would lose it and likely lose the title in short order with CM Punk and Kevin Owens circling.

Penta continues to circle Sami Zayn each week on SmackDown, and WWE cannot keep teasing his inevitable cash-in forever.

Unless WWE sets up a clear rival to keep the luchador busy, that cash-in will happen sooner than later.

If Penta is going to cash in soon, Crown Jewel offers his best opportunity to remain a babyface by defeating the villainous Zayn to become WWE champion.

However, the story of Owens defeating Zayn to regain the top title is a major storyline that WWE cannot ignore.

If Penta dethrones Zayn, it is highly likely that KO would be the one to beat him and certainly before WrestleMania. That is a short time in the spotlight for Penta.

3. Penta Turns Heel by Taking Advantage of a Vulnerable Roman Reigns at Survivor Series

Pro: Penta could not ask for a bigger moment than dethroning Roman Reigns at Survivor Series, and he would instantly become one of WWE's top heels.

Con: Fans are not ready to boo Penta, and it is hard to imagine The OTC losing a rematch for his gold after a cheap cash-in.

A Money in the Bank cash-in is often a heel move, and taking advantage of a beaten-down Reigns after his WarGames match against The 946 would make Penta look unmistakably like a villain.

This could have an impact similar to CM Punk's heel turn following his second cash-in, against Jeff Hardy.

Is Penta ready to be a heel though? The luchador is growing in popularity and represents the future of lucha libre in WWE.

If he is going to carry the legacy of Rey Mysterio forward as WWE's most popular luchador, a heel turn would be a diversion from that goal.

As big a moment as this would be, it would distract from the reason that Penta won the Money in the Bank briefcase in the first place.

It is best not to take a massive swing that could hurt Penta more than help him long term, especially since Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi at WrestleMania 43 is still likely the end goal.

2. Penta Challenges Roman Reigns to a Rematch at WrestleMania 43

Pro: There is no bigger stage in WWE than WrestleMania, and it would be especially appropriate for him to dethrone Roman Reigns after The OTC cost him his biggest match in Mexico City.

Con: Saudi Arabia is not the best place for Penta's first title win, and this would get in the way of Oba Femi's rise to the top of Raw.

All signs point to The OTC remaining dominant all the way to 'Mania where he will face WWE's biggest rising star, Oba Femi.

However, Penta clearly made a lasting impact with his first match against Reigns and could do so again on a bigger stage.

While it has been teased in the past, no one has ever used the Money in the Bank briefcase to call their spot in a 'Mania main event, and it would make sense for Penta to want that.

Is Saudi Arabia the ideal place for this moment? No, especially since the first match between Reigns and Penta was so special because it was in Mexico, but 'Mania is still the biggest show of the year.

While Penta could also take this same approach in calling his shot for the WWE Championship, there is no bigger babyface call Penta could make than saying he is going to beat The OTC at the show he has main evented more than anyone else.

1. Call His Shot at an Undisputed WWE Championship Match in Mexico

Pro: Makes up for Penta not winning the gold in Mexico earlier in the year and creates one of the most important title wins in WWE history in Mexico.

Con: No clear WWE show on the horizon for this moment.

It is not clear yet when WWE will return to Mexico, but there is no better country for Penta to win the world title.

His journey to the top prize began when he fell just short against Roman Reigns in Mexico City in September, supported by a raucous crowd that wanted to see the upset.

Now that Penta holds the Money in the Bank briefcase, he could cash in his contract, but he could also follow the Rob Van Dam path in choosing the best environment for his success.

WWE could even use this to promote AAA by having Penta call his shot for Guerra de Titanes in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico.

WWE could make that AAA show feel must-see by announcing a WWE Championship match for the main event.

It would not necessarily matter who held the championship at that point, but it could be especially appropriate for him to dethrone the first man to win the WWE title in Mexico, Sami Zayn.

Whether it is at a AAA show or he waits until 2027 when WWE next returns to Mexico for a Raw or SmackDown, this is the best option to give Penta an unforgettable babyface win.

articles.title: Re-Grading the Biggest NHL Offseason Trades and Signings After 1 Month Into the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: It's kind of wild to think about all the time we had during the NHL offseason for trades and signings to settle out, and how quickly everyone got thrown into the fire of a new season. And now that season is a month old, and we've got an appetizer of those players in new locations, which gives us plenty of early ammo to judge how they've done.
articles.body:
It's kind of wild to think about all the time we had during the NHL offseason for trades and signings to settle out, and how quickly everyone got thrown into the fire of a new season. And now that season is a month old, and we've got an appetizer of those players in new locations, which gives us plenty of early ammo to judge how they've done.

We're sensitive to how much being a new player in a new situation can be difficult to start, and we'll do our best not to be too harsh, but the play can force the issue, good or bad. It's not quite a report card, so don't sweat showing it to your parents, but just know we're watching closely anyway.

JJ Peterka's arrival in Boston via trade with Utah got him back on the East Coast and playing for fellow German head coach Marco Sturm. That combination of elements, as well as Peterka providing speed and skill to the Bruins lineup, is paying off early on.

Through 12 games, Peterka has four goals and five assists, and while David Pastrňák leads the team in scoring by far with 17 points, Peterka is part of a mass of Boston players supporting him in a big way. After getting beaten by Buffalo in the first round of the playoffs last year due in part to not being as fast as them, Peterka adds that to Boston's lineup without altering the way the team plays.

Peterka's scored 25-plus goals in three straight seasons, and with the style of game he's got and the way the Bruins are playing in general, it's not wrong to think that Peterka could crack 30 goals for the first time in his career (he's on pace for 27).

It's been a very average start to the season for the Blues. Literally.

They're 5-5-1 and in the middle of the pack in the NHL. That said, one of the reasons they've been successful this season is the summertime trade acquisition of Mason McTavish.

McTavish is tied for the team lead in scoring with Dylan Holloway, with 10 points, and his six goals are tied for the team lead with Jimmy Snuggerud. McTavish's no-quit style and up-tempo play have been an ideal fit for the Blues in their new lineup.

His advanced stats are middle of the road but not negative, and if you're hoping for sustainability, those are good signs. That he's on pace for around 45 goals should have Blues fans beyond excited.

There's a lot to like about what Pavel Dorofeyev has shown with the Rangers, but there are causes for concern just the same.

In 14 games, Dorofeyev has three goals and five assists, a pace of 18 goals and 47 points. After signing him to a seven-year, $77 million deal this summer after acquiring his rights from Vegas, that outcome would be a brutal start to his Blueshirts career.

Of course, Dorofeyev is a shooter, and shooters can be streaky. Right now, he's in a cold spell. He's shooting 7.1 percent this season, and coming into this season, his career average was 14.8 percent. Generally, players don't stay cold all season, so things are bound to turn around.

On the flip side, Dorofeyev's bad luck might also mean poor defensive results when he's on the ice, too. His plus-minus rating is minus-13, which ties him with Patrick Kane for the lowest mark in the NHL. We know plus-minus is not a catch-all stat, but when it's a mark that's tied for worst in the league, there's no amount of spinning you can do to make it look better. It's just bad.

The offense will rebound eventually, and the defensive numbers should improve with them. At least the Rangers hope they will.

When Alex Tuch and the Buffalo Sabres couldn't come to terms on keeping the Syracuse-area native in Western New York, the Capitals were more than happy to add him, knowing full well that Alex Ovechkin didn't have many more years left to play. Right now, it looks like they were geniuses, even if they did pay a high price.

Tuch's eight-year, $84 million deal in a sign-and-trade with Buffalo has provided the Capitals with nine points in 10 games (tying him with Dylan Strome for the team lead) as well as a team leading seven goals. His skills have been a natural fit in Washington and have helped the Caps out to a 6-4-0 start, including a 5-2-0 home record.

Tuch has teamed up on a line with Strome and fellow newcomer Jordan Kyrou and if that's how they're going to start the season, maintaining that success will be vital to getting Washington back to the playoffs and being Eastern Conference contenders.

Florida adding Brady Tkachuk to their roster to join his brother Matthew was always going to be a high-profile move and ripe for scrutiny if it didn't work out. Apart from the tough showing in Ottawa on Brady's return to face the team he scorned, things have gone very well for him with the Panthers.

Brady leads the Panthers with seven goals, and he's tied for second on the Panthers in scoring with Seth Jones with 12 points, trailing only his brother Matthew with 16 points. Brady not needing to be a captain in Florida and just focusing on playing hockey is working out quite well for him so far, and it's benefiting the Panthers.

Florida is right in the mix in the middle of everything in the Atlantic Division and Eastern Conference, while going without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, as well as missing goalie Jacob Markström for a spell. Adding Brady to the mix was always going to be a bit of a luxury, but for now it's playing out a little better than expected.

Part of how the Utah Mammoth wanted to build on making the playoffs a year ago was to add more experience and veteran leadership to their extremely talented young core. The easiest way they did that was to add Vincent Trocheck from the New York Rangers.

Trocheck's value to the Mammoth won't necessarily be measured through points and goals, although they do help. His role with Utah is to take on that responsibility to win draws (63.1 percent) and give scorers like Logan Cooley and Dylan Guenther someone to defend strongly on their line.

Trocheck is helping his line maintain the puck and generate shots (56.5 CorsiFor%) as well as facilitating high-quality chances at 5-on-5 (62.8 xGF%). With three goals and four assists in 12 games, on top of the strong advanced numbers, he's off to a very good start while playing a much larger role.

When Bowen Byram let the Buffalo Sabres know he wasn't interested in signing an extension there and was ready to move on to be a No. 1 defenseman elsewhere, the Chicago Blackhawks were more than eager to make that happen.

Chicago took Byram and Jordan Greenway from Buffalo in exchange for the No. 4 pick in the draft, a second-round pick, and Louis Crevier, and then signed Byram to a six-year, $75 million extension to keep him from becoming a free agent. With hopes being sky-high for a turnaround, things could not be going worse for the Blackhawks and Byram.

In six games, Byram has no goals and one assist and has a plus-minus of minus-7. Although his advanced stats are among the best on his team, they're not very good in either shots (45.4 CorsiFor%) or shot quality (40.5 xGF%) at 5-on-5. Meanwhile, the 'Hawks are 3-8-0 to start the season, and there have been little to no signs of improvement even after Connor Bedard's return from injury.

It's early in Byram's Chicago career, and you have to hope this is as tough as it'll be.

When the Panthers brought Jacob Markström back to Florida in a trade with New Jersey to replace Sergei Bobrovsky, the hope was that the veteran would get his mojo back where his career began. The bar Bobrovsky set last season was low to clear, although his legacy with two Stanley Cups also makes it impossibly difficult.

Although Markström is dealing with an injury now, the start of his reunion with Florida has been decent enough. He's 3-1-1 in six games with an .897 save percentage and a shutout. It helps to note that the current league average is .892 for context.

His 2.21 goals-against average is solid, and while the Panthers have had other serious injuries interrupt their aim to return to glory, the play that Markström has provided has given them reason to feel positive about where things can go.

It's easy to forget Markström has had seasons where he was among the best goalies in the league, and once/if the Panthers get back to good health, having him near the top of his game will give them the chance to be in the mix for the Cup again.

During the offseason, one of the biggest shopping list items for the San Jose Sharks was to add experienced defensemen to help push them further up the standings and back into the postseason. Arguably, their biggest addition was Darnell Nurse in a trade with Edmonton.

The move to add Nurse had more detractors than it did supporters, but with the way the Sharks play, a defensive defenseman like Nurse (and Jacob Trouba) was seen as a natural fit. Through 11 games, Nurse has a goal and an assist while playing just over 21 minutes a night. Unfortunately, the Sharks are allowing 3.5 goals per game while scoring 3.0 themselves, and that's never a positive for both the goaltending and defense. In Nurse's case, his 5-on-5 advanced stats are deeply worrying.

Nurse's shot metrics (38.8 CorsiFor%) as well as shot quality (36.0 xGF%) are the worst on the team among regulars. A defenseman playing the kind of minutes he does and spending most of the time seeing tons of shots against and struggling to deny quality opportunities is a major contributing factor to the Sharks' goals-against problem. Better goaltending may help stop some of the goals, but when defense is helping allow so many opportunities, it's an issue that goes deeper.

When the St. Louis Blues moved Jordan Kyrou to Washington in an offseason trade, it gave Kyrou the opportunity to start fresh after a couple of difficult seasons with the Blues. Teaming up with another new Capitals forward is working out well for him and the team all the same.

In 10 games, Kyrou has two goals and six assists (eight points), and he's been able to give the Capitals a dynamic second line with Alex Tuch and Dylan Strome. While Tuch leads the team in goals, Kyrou running and gunning with him and Strome is proving to be difficult for opposing teams to contain, especially when the Caps are at home, where they're 5-2-0.

Although Kyrou was much more of a goal scorer with the Blues, those opportunities are sure to come with Washington. Still, his eight points are tied for second most on the team and just a point behind both of his linemates, who lead the team.

When Sergei Bobrovsky and the Florida Panthers weren't able to work something out, where he landed in free agency was a bit of a mystery. Seeing him land with the Toronto Maple Leafs as part of their massive offseason makeover was somewhat surprising. So far, whatever expectations could be had for his performance have been met...depending on your point of view.

If the hope was to see the Bobrovsky who took over in the postseason for the Panthers and was a world beater, then there's disappointment to be had. If the player we've seen during the regular season the past few years was who you thought you'd see, then you're looking like the smartest person in the room.

Bobrovsky's 3-4-2 record with an .897 save percentage and 3.02 goals-against average is just above league average. Although backup Anthony Stolarz has better save percentage numbers (.907 SV%; 2.79 GAA), the lead job is Bobrovsky's, but the dual setup and the reemergence of Auston Matthews have the Leafs off to a strong start. If Bob can play steady and get Toronto back to the playoffs, the hope of seeing "Playoff Bob" is enough to give the Leafs reason to believe.

Patrick Kane's return to Chicago was celebrated by many Blackhawks fans, and his two-year, $16 million deal to come back and, ideally, help be the veteran guide for a young team to get back to the playoffs was something the player and team were enthusiastic about.

On the one hand, Kane is leading Chicago in scoring with seven points (one goal, six assists) in 11 games. On the downside, he's tied with Rangers forward Pavel Dorofeyev with a minus-13 plus-minus rating for the lowest mark in the NHL. Chicago went without Connor Bedard for the start of the season, so Kane leading them in points so early may not be too big of a surprise. That it's with just seven points while the 'Hawks average 2.18 goals per game is a team-wide concern.

Chicago wasn't signing Kane to compete for the Selke Trophy, but a poor defense metric like plus-minus is one thing, while the advanced numbers at 5-on-5 are also suffering greatly (39.2 CF%; 36.9 xGF%) is another. With team-wide numbers suffering similarly, the issues are well beyond what Kane is doing (or isn't).

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma hits ton as India beat New Zealand by 6 wickets in 3rd T20
articles.summary: The opening pair put on 133-run partnership as India chased down 199 to wrap up the five-match T20 series.
articles.body:
An aggressive partnership between Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi propelled India to a six-wicket win and a series victory over New Zealand in Wellington.

India sewed up the five-match Twenty20 International (T20I) series on Tuesday with two games to spare, chasing down New Zealand’s total of 198 in just 13.2 overs, with Abhishek blasting 113 and Sooryavanshi 45.

The opening pair’s 133-run partnership in just 7.1 overs obliterated the New Zealand bowling attack with one of the most destructive partnerships in T20I history.

Jacob Duffy’s first over went for 26 runs, and the openers never let up.

Abhishek hit nine fours and 11 sixes in his 38-ball knock, receiving a standing ovation when he eventually fell to the bowling of Kyle Jamieson.

By that stage, India had reached 178-2 in just 10 overs.

“The key was pretty simple: Vaibhav and I enjoyed our time,” Abhishek said of their partnership.

“When we were fielding, we saw there was some extra bounce. Vaibhav started off well, and we took the momentum from there.”

Sooryavanshi was promoted to open alongside Abhishek after batting at number three in the second T20I, hitting four fours and four sixes in his 19-ball innings.

“Getting 100 in five overs – I have not seen that before at the international level,” India captain Shreyas Iyer said.

“Credit where it is due, the way they played was exceptional.”

India won the toss for the third time in three matches and again elected to bowl.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Arshdeep Singh extracted prodigious seam from the pitch, beating the outside edge of New Zealand openers Tim Seifert and Finn Allen.

Seifert was removed top-edging Singh for two, before Daryl Mitchell joined Allen and combined for an 86-run partnership.

Mitchell was quick to assess the conditions and moved around the crease to counteract the seam movement.

He seized on any short deliveries with powerful strikes to the short square boundaries, hitting five fours and five sixes on his way to 89 from 52 balls.

Allen made 40 from 25 balls before departing, and Mitchell found another powerful partner in Bevon Jacobs, who hit an unbeaten 39 from 23 deliveries.

The fourth T20I is at Auckland’s Eden Park on Friday.

articles.title: Mitchell Lawrie, 15, eyes £501,000 live TV win over Luke Littler
articles.summary: Mitchell Lawrie, 15, one of 24 amateur players taking part in live TV special Beat Luke Littler, has his sights on a £501,000 bullseye should he beat the world darts champion.
articles.body:
At just 15 years old, Mitchell Lawrie has his sights on a £501,000 bullseye should he beat world darts champion Luke Littler in a potentially life-changing live appearance on national television.

The Renfrew teenager is one of 24 amateur players chosen to take part in Netflix's live special, Beat Luke Littler, which will be broadcast from the Manchester Central Convention Complex on Friday.

Each contestant has the chance to face Littler in a single leg of 501 but the first to beat the 19-year-old two-time world champion will land the big-money prize and bring the competition to an immediate end.

"If someone has already beaten Littler, that's the show done," Lawrie told BBC Radio Scotland Breakfast.

'Beating Luke Littler will change my daughter's life'

Smith holds on to beat Schindler in Euros final

He added: "There's a bundle of good players in there and you're just hoping you get a chance before they get a chance. There's a few big names I want to go before."

Lawrie admits "there's going to be nerves there obviously" and "being live on Netflix at 15 years of age is just something else".

However, he points out: "Everybody there has a chance at the end of the day.

"He is obviously the best player in the world so it may be only one leg of darts but it is a very hard leg to win."

Nevertheless, Lawrie already has a victory over Littler under his belt.

"It was at the World Cup junior darts in Gibraltar in 2023, Scotland against England and we beat the team that Luke Littler was in," he recalls.

"We beat them 4-3 in a deciding leg and it's one of those memories that sticks with you forever.

"We also went on to win that tournament. It is the first time Scotland ever won the World Cup and it was my first year - it was something else.

"It was a surreal experience that I would love to have back."

Indeed, Lawrie was crowned WDF Open Youth World Champion last year before being described as "the future of darts" by Jimmy van Schie after the Dutchman beat the Scot when he became the first teenager to reach the WDF World Championship final in December.

Lawrie, whose inspiration is former world number one Gary Anderson, twice winner of the more prestigious PDC World Darts Championship, says he has been playing darts since his grandfather mounted a board on a chair when he was two years old.

"It just spiralled from there," he says. "But I never took it seriously until three and a half years ago.

"People still want to be a professional footballer, and it was the same for me, but I realised at a young age I wasn't good enough for it so I had to do something else and I just chose darts and I stuck to it and turned out quite good at it."

articles.title: What prompted Matvei Gridin to hit the Griddy after scoring twice against the Toronto Maple Leafs
articles.summary: Calgary Flames' Matvei Gridin scores twice against the Toronto Maple Leafs and celebrates with the Griddy dance, showcasing his personality and connecting with fans.
articles.body: Calgary Flames prospect Matvei Gridin celebrated his second goal against the Toronto Maple Leafs by performing the Griddy, a dance popularized in football. Gridin later explained that his nickname is “Griddy” and that the Calgary team’s three-goal lead made the moment feel right for the celebration.The young forward’s performance combined a productive night on the scoreboard with a spontaneous display of personality. His celebration quickly became a talking point alongside the Flames’ win over Toronto.Matvei Gridin celebrates Calgary Flames’ NHL win over TorontoGridin said the celebration was a natural fit because “Griddy” is his nickname. Rather than planning a choreographed routine, the Calgary Flames prospect decided to dance in the moment, adding a personal touch to his goal celebration.The game situation also played a part. Gridin scored a power-play goal just 25 seconds into the second period, putting Calgary ahead 3–0 against Toronto. With the Flames holding a comfortable lead, he felt there was room to enjoy the moment.That explains the celebration, though, because it was a combination of his nickname, the score and the excitement of scoring. It was not a staged stunt or a message to the opposition.How did Matvei Gridin make an impact against Toronto?Gridin scored two goals against the Maple Leafs, and his offensive contribution was the most important part of his performance, and the Griddy celebration added a memorable moment, but his ability to find the net was the main takeaway for Calgary.Scoring twice against an Original Six franchise also gave the young forward a chance to get noticed. For a young player trying to break into the NHL, big games can do wonders for his confidence and show he can contribute at the top level.The power-play goal that made it 3–0 showed Gridin could capitalize on a special-teams opportunity, and his second goal gave the night another highlight, while the celebration helped his performance reach a wider audience beyond the game itself.What is the Griddy dance and why did it attract attention?The Griddy is a celebratory dance that was made popular through football. Especially after NFL players like Justin Jefferson made it popular. The routine usually involves rhythmic steps, arm motions and facial gestures. It has since spread to other sports as athletes have taken it up to celebrate big moments.In hockey, goal celebrations frequently involve teammates, familiar gestures, or spontaneous outbursts of excitement, and Gridin’s choice was distinctive as it introduced a recognizable football celebration to the rink, directly tying into his nickname.It also showed a lighter side of the NHL prospect. The young players are often evaluated on their stats, consistency and development. But personality can also help them connect with fans. Gridin found a way to celebrate in a way that was memorable, but didn’t steal the spotlight from his two-goal performance.But for Calgary supporters, the priority will be on his progress as a player and his ability to keep contributing offensively. Should Gridin keep banging in goals, fans might see more celebrations in the future. In the meantime, his game against the Toronto also offered up a decent contribution on the ice as well as an impromptu moment that gave the NHL one more entertaining highlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Connor Hellebuyck’s trade happened when it did, and how keeping quiet may have shaped the entire deal
articles.summary: Connor Hellebuyck’s departure from the Winnipeg Jets was not just about an unpaid suspension or the money the team owed him.
articles.body: Connor Hellebuyck’s departure from the Winnipeg Jets was not just about an unpaid suspension or the money the team owed him. The timing also reflected a growing concern that the dispute could become more damaging if it spilled into public view. NHL insider Elliotte Friedman offered that explanation on Monday’s edition of the 32 Thoughts Podcast, suggesting the Jets wanted to avoid a public exchange between the goaltender and the organization. With tensions already high, the club had reasons to settle the situation before Hellebuyck could address the media. The move was about limiting further damage, not simply moving a player.The Jets wanted to avoid a public confrontationThe initial explanation for the timing centered on Hellebuyck’s unpaid suspension and the prospect of him returning to the team and collecting his salary. Friedman, however, pointed to another concern: the possibility that the goaltender would speak publicly about the situation.“There was a chance that Hellebuyck was going to talk to the media, that he was going to make himself available. And look, regardless of what anyone feels about all this, and who they think is right and who they think is wrong and whatever, while this has caused incredible strain on everyone involved, people were trying to be respectful of each other.”That concern changed the picture. If Hellebuyck had spoken before a trade, his account of the dispute could have prompted a response from Winnipeg. The organization might then have found itself answering questions about an increasingly tense relationship instead of focusing on hockey.Friedman made the potential consequences clear. “I think if Hellebuyck had spoken, the gloves would have gone off. And I think the Jets would have responded in kind.”Neither side had much to gain from a public back-and-forth. Once competing accounts entered the conversation, the dispute could have become harder to contain. A trade offered Winnipeg a way to end that immediate uncertainty before it grew into a larger distraction.Player concerns added pressure to the decisionThe Jets also had to consider the mood inside their own dressing room. Friedman reported that general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff met with the team's leadership group in Dallas to discuss the next steps. Captain Adam Lowry was among the leaders who wanted the situation put behind them.“(Kevin) Cheveldayoff met with his leadership group in Dallas, and they talked about what the next steps were; I think the team knew how the players felt. I just think the organization said, ‘it’s time. It is time to do this and the time is now.’”That detail matters because it suggests the decision was not driven by management alone. The unresolved situation had become a concern for the wider group, making a quick resolution more appealing.The Winnipeg Jets also had the Heritage Classic to consider. Carrying an unsettled dispute into the event risked pulling attention away from the team and its hockey commitments.Money remained part of the equation, but Friedman described the strain of having Hellebuyck return to the team as a bigger issue. The timing, then, reflected several pressures at once: salary concerns, the risk of a public dispute and a dressing room ready to move forward. Winnipeg chose to act before those pressures became harder to manage.The trade did not erase the tension that led to it. It did, however, give the organization a chance to move on without another public confrontation dominating the story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe apologises after ‘dictator’ comment angers Chinese fans
articles.summary: ‘My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people,’ Mbappe says after Chinese brands dropped him.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe has apologised for his “ill-judged” comment linked to Mao Zedong that angered Chinese football fans and cost him at least two sponsors in the country.

The French football star was dropped by two major brands in China on Tuesday after a video circulated online in which the French football superstar apparently joked about a former Chinese leader.

While Mbappe did not name Mao in the video, he appeared to say the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face digitally altered onto that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

“My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” Mbappe wrote in a statement published on his social media accounts.

The 27-year-old said he “reacted to an image of myself” during the interview.

“I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” Mbappe went on to add. “This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.”

The statement was published in French, Mandarin and English.

The video, which shows Mbappe preparing to go on air, was purportedly filmed in April, as verified by Al Jazeera.

The clip was shared by French football podcast The Bridge and widely circulated on social media on Monday.

The maelstrom caused by the Real Madrid forward’s comments prompted La Liga to issue an apology on behalf of the league and the club.

The Spanish league condemned and apologised to China over the remarks after the player was dropped by two Chinese brands.

“La Liga deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga,” the league said in a statement.

La Liga president Javier Tebas issued an apology on X and said that the organisation deeply ⁠⁠regretted the alleged comments that “have caused discomfort and offence in China”.

“We are taking the measures within our reach and working directly with our partners and interlocutors in China to overcome this situation,” Tebas wrote. “A relationship built over so many years cannot be damaged by a single episode.”

Chinese drinks giant Dongpeng has terminated its contract with Mbappe “with immediate effect”.

“Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” it said in a statement.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with Mbappe, who until this incident was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media.

In China, satire or jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who ruled it from 1949 until his death in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

“A remark about an internet meme has triggered a backlash among his Chinese fans, threatened his lucrative commercial relationships and offered a sharp reminder of the ‌‌limits of celebrity influence,” state media outlet China Daily said.

Mbappe – one of the world’s most prominent athletes who has ties to firms from sportswear brand On Holding to hotel chain Accor and toy maker Lego – became the latest sports star to fall foul of a faux pas in China.

Many Chinese media outlets condemned Mbappe’s apparent remarks, but did not repeat them.

“What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it,” the state-backed Global Times said.

“The message from Chinese consumers is clear: Respect is not optional; one doesn’t get to profit from China while disrespecting it. Not a chance.”

China’s state television has halted broadcasts of all matches and events involving La Liga and Mbappe, and all advertisements involving Mbappe have been removed, the state-backed media outlet The Paper reported on Tuesday.

As of 07:00 GMT, four topics related to Mbappe were still among the top 10 trending searches on China’s social media platform Weibo. Some netizens called for China to “blacklist” Mbappe and reduce his commercial value to zero. These comments received hundreds of likes.

When asked about ‌‌the ‌‌incident, a spokesperson for China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people “will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society”.

articles.title: Report: Bearman’s Salary Demand Has Slowed Talks of F1 2027 Renewal with Haas
articles.summary: Oliver Bearman’s reported salary demand has slowed down the F1 renewal talks between his management, Ferrari and Haas. After the departure of Esteban Ocon, H...
articles.body:
Oliver Bearman's reported salary demand has slowed down the F1 renewal talks between his management, Ferrari and Haas.

After the departure of Esteban Ocon , Haas confirmed Ferrari junior and F2 graduate Rafael Camara as his replacement for the 2027 F1 season. Interestingly, they did not confirm Bearman as his teammate, even though it is certain it will be him.

Even at the F1 US GP, Bearman left it to his management and Ferrari to decide. "I think on our side as well, if I'm not mistaken, we're very sure that we want to continue working together, and the only sticking points are kind of out of my hands, more contractual points," said Bearman to the media.

"I want to get a lot from them, but no, it's out of my hands, I am leaving it to my management and, of course, Ferrari as well." Following the statement, a report from business F1 writer Marc Limacher has noted the sticking point.

Business Writer Points at Bearman's Deamnds

He has highlighted the salary demand of Bearman to be six million euros, which Haas doesn't wish to pay – which in turn has slowed down the renewal talks. The Brit, who will be the senior pro in F1 2027, insists he is committed to the American team.

The length of the deal is not in his hands, but the desire is naturally to fight for podiums and wins. He hopes he can do it with Haas, but if he cannot, he is not shy about targeting the Top 4 teams. As he is a Ferrari F1 junior, it is a natural move.

However, Charles Leclerc has signed a long-term deal, and Lewis Hamilton is most likely to stay for the 2027 F1 season and possibly 2028 too. "I'm committed to Haas myself, and the length of the deal is not really my remit," said Bearman.

Bearman Feels Ready for Step Up But Committed to Haas

"I'm happy to be in F1, but of course, looking into the medium-to-long term, I also feel like I'm ready to fight for podiums and fight at the front. In terms of a midfield team, Haas is the team that I want to be with, and I see my future with.

"But at some point, as well, I feel like I've earned the opportunity to go out and look for a top four team. And of course, with my link with Ferrari, that would be my ultimate goal. But yeah, as I said, I'm not discussing the nitty-gritty. That's what my kind of short-term ambition is, and my medium-to-long-term is, of course, to be fighting for podiums.

"I hope that Haas can give me that opportunity, but yeah, let's see. Of course, Ferrari is involved. At the end, I am a junior driver of Ferrari, and that's ultimately the reason I'm here because of that. So, of course, they have a big say in what my future looks like," summed up Bearman, who knows that the 2027 F1 season will likely be a shootout.

With Camara joining Haas as a rookie, Ferrari will have a chance to directly compare the two F1 drivers in the same machinery, which will help them make the best decision. The shootout will most likely be for Hamilton's seat, and Bearman is aware.

articles.title: How J.J. Sullinger's gift of a kidney saved fellow Buckeye Terence Dials
articles.summary: Former Ohio State Buckeye Terence Dials was in need of a kidney transplant. His former teammate, J.J. Sullinger, answered the call. Here's how.
articles.body:
James Sullinger, who played at Ohio State during the Thad Matta era and helped revive the program's fortunes, has always had a way with words.

Once, during his four-year tenure, the former Buckeye more commonly known as "J.J." entertained with a story about why he wore scarlet tights as part of his uniform, claiming he felt the chill of the ice at the Schottenstein Center seeping through its hardwood covering. As the Buckeyes were finishing off a Cinderella run to the 2006 Big Ten title , he told reporters, "They hate us because they ain't us."

Yes, outspoken and possessing a megawatt smile, Sullinger has always had a way with words.

The word brotherhood? He was part of a group of players that long described each other as brothers, but it hits a little differently for him now.

On Oct. 12, Sullinger and best friend and former teammate Terence Dials checked into the hospital for a kidney donation. Sullinger was the donor, Dials the recipient. The two men met as adversaries in AAU basketball during high school and quickly became best friends in college. They now share a bond that goes deeper than any platitudes about brotherhood.

It took a year's worth of work for Sullinger to be able to save Dials' life . Asked to describe what that brotherhood means to him now, Sullinger had to compose himself and grasped at an answer.

"Words don't really do it justice, so when I tell you I knew I was going to do this, it just doesn't hit for me the way it should," he said. "The best way for me to explain this is Terence has always been a brother to me. My dad calls him [his] No. 4 [son]. It's always been like that. This just solidifies it. I don't like taking the credit because I just feel like this is something I was supposed to do. If I was able to do it, I was going to do it.

"I'm just grateful that I was able to do it."

Dials knew he was on this trajectory for roughly a decade. During the time when he was playing professionally, a routine medical checkup revealed slightly elevated creatinine levels, which led to a referral to a nephrologist. Kidneys don't repair themselves once their production starts to decline, so the best he could hope for was to keep things stable as long as possible with a combination of diet and exercise.

It was about five years ago that Dials' doctor told him a transplant was inevitable. During the summer of 2025, his Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) was low enough that Dials was placed on the national transplant list. He received a link to a website that he could share with anyone he wanted, hoping it would speed up the process of finding a compatible and willing donor.

"I told my family and friends and I just remember J.J. being like, 'I want to do this,' " Dials said. "He was like the first one to jump at it. I had two immediate matches with my brother (Michael) and J.J. That's how the process started with us."

It took less than two weeks for Sullinger to be identified as a match. He signed up so quickly that he belatedly realized he hadn't even discussed it with his wife, who gave her wholehearted approval regardless.

Finding a match and being cleared for surgery were two distinctly different milestones in the process.

Dials was informed that he had received two matches, but the hospital could not share the identities of the potential donors. His brother and Sullinger chose to keep Dials abreast of the latest developments.

That included the two men submitting to tests, scans and all kinds of bloodwork to minimize the risk for complications on either side. In Sullinger's case, there were a few causes for concern. Tests showed he was prediabetic and his blood pressure was high enough that he was forced to make some lifestyle changes in an effort to get to a place where he could be deemed healthy enough to donate.

"I stopped drinking alcohol," he said. "They didn't ask me to do that, but I felt like I needed to. I started really focusing on getting my heartrate up in the gym as opposed to just lifting weights. Diet too. But the biggest thing they asked me to do was start getting more rest. I've really been concentrating on my sleep and trying to get [at least] eight hours a night."

In essence, Sullinger trained for a year to be allowed to donate. At one point, Sullinger wore a portable blood pressure machine for 48 hours that randomly checked him and recorded the results. He also learned that he had two other good friends also in need of kidney transplants.

"I hope that this story is told in a way that helps someone or catapults someone to consider donating or somebody telling their story so they're made aware that they need a kidney," he said. "I think it's important to talk about."

In late September, more than a year after Dials first started his search for a donor, Sullinger got a simple email informed him all tests were done and they could move forward. He followed up: Did this mean they could schedule the surgery?

Once he got his reply, Sullinger sent Dials a text telling him he was going to stop by the Schottenstein Center to see him. Hired as director of professional development for the men's basketball team in 2019, Dials is now starting his third season as the program's recruiting coordinator. His former teammate frequently stopped by to check on the current team, so Dials had no idea about the news he was about to receive.

At the arena where they once played together, Sullinger delivered the news face-to-face.

"I'm like, 'I'm full-go, baby. It's time,' " Sullinger said. "He was shocked. We looked at each other and he won't tell you he was crying, but I know he was crying. It was a special moment between two brothers, man. We got a chance to hug it out, dap up and solidify the start of all of this."

Said Dials: "We embraced each other and hugged. We were in shock a little bit."

The surgery took place Oct. 12 at University of Cincinnati hospital. What Dials said felt like five minutes to him was roughly a five-hour procedure, and when he woke up in the recovery room, he learned something surprising about his new kidney.

"The lady came in and she said, 'I don't know if you're into scientific stuff but once the doctor put in the kidney, it started pumping blood going through immediately,' " he said. "That's not normal. Normally it takes a while for the blood to start circulating through. She was amazed by it."

Before long, both donor and recipient made their way back home to begin the recovery process. For Dials, that has meant a lot of isolation, rest and doctor's appointments. While on medication to prevent transplant rejection, Dials said his immune system is compromised to the point where he's not allowed to be in contact with anyone under the age of 14 because they have not had all their necessary vaccinations yet.

He's allowed to take walks around his neighborhood, but his only other trips are to visit his doctor. While there, he has to wear a mask. Every day, Dials has to report his blood pressure, temperature and weight multiple times. His hope is to be back at work sometime in December.

Sullinger said because they went through his abdominal muscles to remove the kidney, he has little core strength at the moment but otherwise, he is feeling better day by day. He was among a group of about 20 former players in attendance for Ohio State's home exhibition game against Butler on Oct. 25, there to see Matta, who was being recognized at halftime for his offseason retirement and 502 career victories.

When Matta was given the microphone, neither Sullinger nor Dials, who was watching from home, knew what was about to happen.

"Maybe the greatest thing I've seen in my coaching career happened a few weeks ago," Matta told the crowd. "A few weeks ago, James Sullinger gave his kidney to his teammate, Terence Dials."

Standing off to the edge of the group, Sullinger said he momentarily blacked out while covering his face as the emotions washed over him. At home, Dials said he couldn't hear what Matta said but had a pretty good idea by Sullinger's reaction.

"Coach Matta, man. He has a funny way of never making it about him," Sullinger said.

Both men had been in frequent communication with Matta and his wife, Barbara, but neither knew he was going to talk about the transplant. With the news now public, Dials and Sullinger said their phones quickly began to light up with messages of support.

The outpouring has been humbling, Dials said.

"As of [Matta's speech], Buckeye Nation stepped up and started sending me all types of messages via social media or the ones that have my phone number reached out," he said. "To all the people who stepped up, I thank them. It's great that Buckeye Nation is getting behind us."

The timing of it all resonated with Dials on another personal level. Exactly one year to the day of the Butler game, former Ohio State football player Nick Mangold passed away at the age of 41 shortly after publicly disclosing a battle with kidney disease. When he passed, Dials said it emphasized the situation he was in and the hope for a donor sooner rather than later.

"That's a peer of mine who I went to school with," Dials said. "I knew him. He dealt with the same thing and when he had a cry for help at the 12th hour, that really hit home that that could happen to me if I don't get a kidney. That was a reality punch, a gut punch like, 'Man, I hope one of these go through.' "

Only two individuals tested were found to be a match for Dials. It might have happened in time, but his brother was ultimately never cleared to donate.

"The real hero of this story is J.J.," he said. "I'm just the recipient. He's the one who had a selfless act. This is the most selfless act you can do. If anything, he's the hero in this, and I want him to get all the accolades and praise because this is what he deserves. He did not have to do it, and he did. Thank him.

"Words aren't enough for what he did for me."

Maybe this time, one word is sufficient: brotherhood.
