articles.title: Former Illini Dosunmu, Shannon Jr. off to strong starts with Timberwolves
articles.summary: Big starts for the Illini greats.
articles.body:
Two former Illinois basketball stars are making an early impact for the Minnesota Timberwolves as Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon Jr. help the team get off to a hot start in the 2026-27 NBA season.

Minnesota won its first three games by at least 20 points before falling just short in a 127-125 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday night.

Dosunmu has been a valuable contributor off the bench, providing scoring and playmaking for the Timberwolves. The former Illini guard scored 16 points in Minnesota's season-opening win over Miami before recording 14 points, seven rebounds and nine assists against Orlando.

Through four games, Dosunmu is averaging 12 points, 4.5 rebounds and four assists per game while shooting efficiently from the field.

Shannon has also gotten off to an encouraging start. The former Illinois star has scored in double figures in all four games, including a 15-point performance against Toronto on Sunday.

The third-year forward followed that outing with 14 points, four rebounds and five assists against Cleveland. Shannon is averaging 13 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game while shooting 14-of-27 from the field.

Both players are carving out important roles for a Minnesota team with significant aspirations in the Western Conference. Dosunmu's versatility and playmaking have made him a productive option off the bench, while Shannon has provided another scoring threat.

articles.title: Michelle Steilen revives roller skating with Moxi
articles.summary: Discover how Michelle Steilen inspires female skaters through Moxi Roller Skates and daring tricks.
articles.body:
Roller skating is more than a sport for Michelle Steilen, also known as Estro Jen, it is a way to express creativity, build confidence, and connect with others. As the founder of Moxi Roller Skates, she is helping introduce a new generation to the excitement of skating on four wheels. Through innovative skate designs and an energetic community of female skaters, Steilen is encouraging people to explore what they can achieve on wheels. Her work combines athletic performance, personal expression, and a passion for bringing roller skating back into the spotlight. For her and the Moxi Skate Team, skating is about chasing dreams and experiencing the freedom of movement.

Steilen developed a deep love for roller skating and wanted to share that passion with people everywhere. She noticed that traditional roller skating had lost some of its popularity as rollerblading became more common. During this shift, innovation in traditional roller skates slowed down, leaving fewer developments designed specifically for creative skating styles. Rather than accepting this decline, Steilen decided to help revive the activity and create new opportunities for skaters to explore their abilities.

Through Moxi Roller Skates, she has helped promote a style of skating that goes beyond simply moving around a rink. The focus includes experimentation, artistic movement, daring tricks, and discovering new ways to use roller skates. Moxi has developed a worldwide team of 21 skaters, including performers known as Pigeon, Indy Jamma Jones, Millie, and Legs. Together, these skaters demonstrate how roller skating can become a platform for athletic achievement and individual creativity.

The equipment itself plays an important role in this movement. According to Steilen, traditional roller skating equipment had not always kept pace with the changing needs of modern skaters. Roller derby brought renewed attention to the sport, but skates designed for derby were primarily built for speed and competition. The skates being developed for Moxi's style of skating focus on different demands, including secure landings and performing high-flying tricks. These features help skaters pursue more challenging movements while developing their skills.

One of the most exciting changes Steilen has witnessed is the increasing ambition of female roller skaters. Moves that once seemed unusual or nearly impossible, including backflips on wheels, are now being performed by women who continue to push the boundaries of the sport. Watching these developments has also changed Steilen's understanding of her own physical abilities. She expresses amazement at what her body can accomplish through practice, determination, and confidence.

For Steilen, the experience of skating goes far beyond technical skill. She describes feeling energised when skating alongside other women, finding motivation in their shared passion and achievements. The community provides an environment where participants can encourage each other, experiment with new ideas, and pursue goals that might once have seemed out of reach. This sense of belonging is an important part of what makes skating meaningful to her.

articles.title: Golfers Should Stop Apologizing For Skills, Wagers And Pace
articles.summary: MyGolfSpy reports golfers should quit apologizing for bad shots, declining bets, or playing from shorter tees to enjoy the game without guilt.
articles.body:
Golf culture often demands unnecessary apologies for actions that do not inconvenience anyone on the course. From bad shots to declining side bets, players feel compelled to explain ordinary preferences. MyGolfSpy reported on Tuesday that these apologies stem from misplaced guilt rather than actual rules of etiquette. The outlet argues that paying to play grants a right to enjoy the game without constant disclaimers.

Many golfers introduce themselves with a disclaimer about their handicap before the first tee. This habit aims to lower expectations and reassure strangers of their limitations. However, the pressure to apologize for a topped drive or a three-putt is unfounded. Even the best golfers in the world simply want their playing partners to move things along. Speed of play matters more than perfect execution. A bad shot does not require a public statement or a formal apology for taking up space.

Sports gambling has flooded advertising, yet not every golfer wants money on the line. MyGolfSpy detailed an instance where an influencer announced a $100 per nine wager without asking for handicaps or even introducing himself. This aggressive approach alienates players who prefer a casual round. A competitive round is possible without wagering any money on the game. Declining to participate in a gamble is a valid choice that requires no justification.

Some players feel guilty about moving up a tee box to make the round more enjoyable. MyGolfSpy highlighted this common hesitation with a specific sentiment from a player. The outlet noted that players often say, "I usually play farther back, but …" before explaining their choice. The analysis states that you do not need the rest of that sentence. Playing from a forward tee to maintain pace or increase fun is a legitimate preference. It does not diminish the challenge for others unless the course rules forbid it.

The pressure to apologize often stems from a fear of being judged by better players. This mindset ignores the reality that golf is a game of mistakes for everyone. A player who apologizes for a bunker escape attempt might actually be slowing down the group by overthinking. The focus should remain on being a decent person and playing quickly. Etiquette rules exist to prevent disruption, not to police skill levels or personal preferences. When a player pays for a green fee, they have earned the right to play without shame.

MyGolfSpy suggests that ordinary preferences started requiring explanations somewhere along the way. This shift created a culture where golfers feel guilty for things that inconvenience no one. The outlet lists seven specific areas where this apology culture is unnecessary. These include not being very good at golf, declining to gamble, and moving up a tee box. By removing these mental barriers, the game becomes more accessible and enjoyable. The goal is to have fun, not to perform a perfect round for an audience.

Players should stop explaining why they want to finish in four hours instead of five. They should also stop justifying why they do not want to bet on the outcome of a hole. The course is a place for recreation, not a courtroom where every action needs a defense. As MyGolfSpy points out, the only real rule is to keep the game moving and be a good sport.

articles.title: Nikola Jokic doubles down on ripping Nuggets fans booing team’s struggles

Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets are having a rough start to the season, falling to 1-2 after losing to the Golden State Warriors , 134-114, at Ball Arena on Monday.

The Nuggets looked lackluster in the second half, allowing the Warriors to pull away and get their first win of the season.

After the Nuggets came from behind to beat the New Orleans Pelicans in overtime, 141-135, at home on Saturday, Jokic called out their fans for booing .

articles.title: Wales call up in-form Page after Dyer injury blow
articles.summary: Wales release Rio Dyer from their Nations Championship squad after hamstring injury, with Scarlets wing Macs Page added for November's games.
articles.body:
Dragons wing Rio Dyer has been released from the Wales squad for the Nations Championship because of a hamstring injury, with uncapped Scarlets back Mac Page called up.

Dyer was recalled by head coach Steve Tandy after a strong start to the season, but suffered an injury in the process of scoring against Ospreys last weekend.

The 26-year-old faces a spell on the sidelines and has been released to rehabilitate with the Rodney Parade club.

Dyer won the most recent of his 24 caps against South Africa last autumn and missed out on the Six Nations and summer squads.

His misfortune opens the door for uncapped Page, who is called up despite a head injury suffered for Scarlets at Stormers last Saturday.

Page scored his fifth try of the season in Cape Town but then hit his head heavily on the ground when attempting to get his sixth.

The 21-year-old was given oxygen as he was helped from the field and will go through the return-to-play protocols before pushing for a first cap.

He joins Scarlets team-mates Ellis Mee and Blair Murray as an option in the back three along with Louis Rees-Zammit, Tom Rogers, Josh Adams and Gabriel Hamer-Webb.

Page, who can also play at outside centre, was a member of Wales' touring party to Japan in 2025 but did not feature.

Wales play Japan in Cardiff on Saturday, 7 November and then host New Zealand and Australia.

Tandy's side then take on another southern hemisphere opponent on Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium at the end of the month.

articles.title: Justin Herbert’s fiancée Madison Beer heckled by Chargers fan

articles.body:
It has been a rough year, as the Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6, and some fans are heckling Justin Herbert 's fiancée, Madison Beer, as a result.

articles.title: Colorado insider claims Deion Sanders has offered critics $50,000 to not talk about him
articles.summary: As the fourth year of the Deion Sanders experiment in Colorado continues to collapse, a man with unique access to Coach Prime has made an eye-opening claim.
articles.body:
As the fourth year of the Deion Sanders experiment in Colorado continues to collapse, a man with unique access to Coach Prime has made an eye-opening claim.

Christopher Neely, better known as "Uncle Neely," has served as Deion's personal videographer . Via Essentially Sports , Neely recently said that Sanders has offered cash to his critics in an effort to get them to leave him alone.

"For the most part, the people that attack him wouldn't be making the money they were making if he wasn't here to attack," Neely said earlier this week. "Which is why he told some of them, 'Hey man, let's just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year .' And ain't nobody took the deal yet. . . . And you love talking about this man so much, and you make so much talking of this man that you turned the deal down."

Sanders has yet to confirm or deny Neely's contention. If true, it's stunning. And it's good to know that no one in the media has accepted the offer. It would violate any and all standards of journalism — if basic standards of journalism are still being widely practiced.

It also underscores the extreme level of sensitivity that Sanders has to criticism. Which, while not new for him, continues to be confounding.

How can so many people who have won at the game of life become so bothered by the basic scrutiny, and criticism, that comes with the territory? Nowadays, anyone and everyone with a public profile gets criticized somewhere. The only sensible approach is to ignore it. And, if for whatever reason the person being criticized is tormented by the possibility that they're not universally beloved, the best play is to not give oxygen to the critics by acknowledging it.

First, it only invites more criticism. Second, it makes the person who should otherwise ignore the criticism seem petty, small, and focused on all the wrong things.

Which, in Sanders's case, could help explain why the 2026 season continues to disintegrate. The only question left to answer at this point is whether he'll get a fifth year in Boulder or a buyout.

articles.summary: Florida State coach Mike Norvell plans to lean on younger players to spark the roster vs. Clemson on Halloween. Here's who should we keep an eye on.
articles.body:
As Florida State football (3-4, 1-2 ACC) returns from its bye week and prepares for a Halloween night matchup against Clemson, coach Mike Norvell says the Seminoles could lean more heavily on younger players as they evaluate the depth of the roster and look for a spark in the season's final stretch.

During Monday's press conference , Norvell said several underclassmen used last week's practices to make a strong impression and could see increased opportunities when Clemson (4-3, 2-2) visits Doak Campbell Stadium on Oct. 31.

"I truly believe that they've stayed focused on the things they control and their growth and improvement," Norvell said. "I'm excited to watch them play this week, but we've got to have a great week of preparation. It was good to have those practices last week.

FSU football vs Miami Hurricanes: Photos from ACC rivalry game

"Some guys might have increased roles. Guys a little further down the depth chart got some extra work to continue showing where they are. It was an aggressive week of practice, and I thought the guys handled that well."

Here are six young Seminoles who could see expanded roles against Clemson:

FSU's running back depth has taken a hit following the season-ending injury to Ousmane Kromah and with Samuel Singleton Jr. still unavailable.

That could create a larger role for true freshman Amari Thomas behind starter Tre Wisner. Coaches and teammates have consistently praised Thomas' explosiveness and long-term potential.

The Blountstown native has appeared in four games and recorded three carries, but his workload could increase significantly as the Seminoles look for additional production in the backfield.

Norvell indicated Monday that true freshman wide receiver Devin Carter could make his long-awaited debut if he avoids any health-related setbacks this week.

"Devin Carter, I think, is coming into having an opportunity this week, once again barring any setbacks," Norvell said. "We'll see where that goes and what that looks like, but he continues to be another explosive player that brings opportunity."

Carter impressed during spring practice and appeared poised to contribute immediately as a freshman before a back injury and bruised ribs sidelined him.

If healthy, he could provide another playmaking option for FSU's offense against Clemson.

Norvell specifically highlighted freshman receiver Jasen Lopez after a key reception in FSU's loss to Miami for a 39-yard gain.

"I was really pleased with Jasen Lopez having a big catch in the Miami game," Norvell said. "He's getting a little bit more work there. I thought he had a good week of practice last week as well."

While Duce Robinson, Micahi Danzy and Jayvan Boggs remain the primary receiving targets, Lopez continues to emerge as another reliable option for quarterback Ashton Daniels. He also could contribute on special teams as a punt returner.

Linebacker depth remains a concern with Blake Nichelson unavailable and Omar Graham Jr. suffering an injury against Miami.

That could open the door for freshman linebacker Karon Maycock, who has appeared in five games and recorded four tackles this season.

Most of his defensive production came against Central Arkansas, and he has primarily contributed on special teams. Still, the circumstances could create a larger defensive role if FSU remains short-handed at linebacker.

FSU's cornerback group has battled injuries throughout the season, and Quindarrius Jones' availability has fluctuated in recent weeks.

As a result, Nehemiah Chandler could continue seeing increased snaps on the outside. Defensive coordinator Tony White recently praised Chandler for making critical plays despite limited opportunities.

The former Wakulla High and South Alabama standout has provided valuable depth, totaling nine tackles, one interception and two pass breakups in seven games this season.

Freshman safety Jordan Crutchfield is another player Norvell believes could be ready to contribute.

The 6-foot-3, 218-pound defensive back has appeared in four games, but injuries have limited his consistency throughout the season.

"Jordan's a guy that has shown some flashes here," Norvell said. "He's just dealt with some minor injuries that have kind of set him back in terms of the consistency of his opportunities. But I'm expecting him to get some good work here this week and hopefully be available."

If healthy, Crutchfield could add depth at safety and continue building toward a larger role in FSU's defense.

articles.title: Steelers climb in ESPN NFL power rankings
articles.summary: The Steelers saw a little bump in the ESPN NFL power rankings for Week 8 but still find themselves stuck in the middle of the pack.
articles.body:
If the playoffs started this week, the Pittsburgh Steelers would be among the Wild Card teams in the AFC. The team is currently 5-2 and riding a three-game win streak headed into a huge AFC North match this weekend with the North-leading Cleveland Browns .

Heading into Week 8, ESPN has updated its NFL power rankings and the Steelers got a bump from No. 17 to No. 14 after a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris.

ESPN NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler also noted that he believes the team's biggest offseason addition was cornerback Asante Samuel Jr. Here's what he had to say about it.

Both of the Steelers' starting cornerbacks, Samuel and Jamel Dean, have made big plays this season. But Samuel has turned a modest one-year, $4 million deal into a solidified role. Part of the reason Pittsburgh was comfortable trading cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to Dallas was because of Samuel, who has parlayed a stellar offseason into seven pass deflections through seven games. He has successfully rebuilt his career after undergoing spinal fusion surgery in April 2025.

Not sure I'd call re-signing Samuel as an addition but we cannot deny the impact he is having after the Joey Porter Jr. trade. We would also be remiss if we didn't acknowledge that the biggest addition of the offseason for the Steelers is probably new head coach Mike McCarthy.

The Cleveland Browns are up to No. 16 from No. 19 and the Steelers square off with the Browns this weekend in Pittsburgh.

articles.title: What happened to Brady Tkachuk’s charity pledge after Ottawa Senators fans threw 37 jerseys onto the ice
articles.summary: Brady Tkachuk's plan to donate jerseys thrown by Ottawa Senators fans backfires as many are damaged, highlighting his strained relationship with the fanbase after his trade to the Florida Panthers.
articles.body: Brady Tkachuk’s pledge to donate jerseys thrown onto the ice to BGC Ottawa will not be fulfilled as originally intended because many of the 37 sweaters collected after his return to Ottawa were reportedly damaged or unusable. The incident followed a hostile reception for the former Senators captain during his first visit with the Florida Panthers.The jersey protest reflected lingering frustration among some Ottawa fans following Tkachuk’s departure. What began as a charitable idea tied to the NHL forward’s return has instead become another talking point surrounding his relationship with the Senators fan base.How Brady Tkachuk’s Florida Panthers return sparked an NHL jersey protestBrady Tkachuk’s first game back in Ottawa as a Florida Panthers player became controversial when fans threw 37 of his No. 7 jerseys onto the ice. According to reporting by TSN and Sportsnet, the jerseys were intended to be collected for a donation to BGC Ottawa, but many were too damaged to be given to children.Tkachuk announced his plan before the October 21 game on Wingmen, the podcast he co-hosts with his brother and Florida Panthers teammate Matthew Tkachuk. He said the jerseys thrown onto the ice would be donated to the Boys and Girls Club of Ottawa, now known as BGC Ottawa.The idea offered a charitable purpose for an anticipated show of fan frustration. Tkachuk acknowledged that he expected an emotional reception at Canadian Tire Centre but suggested that any jerseys tossed onto the ice could still benefit young people in Ottawa.The pledge followed a difficult offseason in which Tkachuk requested a trade and left the Senators to join the Panthers. His departure was particularly significant because he had served as Ottawa’s captain and spent eight seasons with the organization.Why can’t the 37 jerseys be donated?Ian Mendes, the Senators’ vice president of communications, confirmed in his October 26 column that 37 jerseys had been collected after the game. He contacted Florida’s organization to share the final count because Tkachuk had expressed interest in making the donation. However, many of the sweaters were damaged or unusable, so they will not be physically passed on to BGC Ottawa.The condition of the jerseys created an unexpected obstacle for the charitable plan. Although the total number was recorded, the collected items could not be distributed to children as originally intended.The development does not necessarily mean that Tkachuk cannot support BGC Ottawa through another contribution. The available report confirms that the jerseys themselves will not be handed over, but it does not establish whether an alternative donation has been arranged.How did Ottawa Senators fans react to Brady Tkachuk’s return?The 37 jerseys became a visible expression of frustration among some Senators supporters following Tkachuk’s offseason departure. His return in a Panthers uniform had attracted attention before the game, with boos and hostile reactions accompanying his appearance at his former home arena.Tkachuk had recorded 463 points in 572 regular-season games for Ottawa, according to Sportsnet, and spent five seasons as captain. His departure therefore marked a major change for a franchise and fan base with which he had been closely associated.The Panthers won the game 5-1, according to the supplied report, while the jersey protest added another layer to an already emotional reunion. The donation setback has since shifted attention from the on-ice result to the consequences of the fans’ response.For Tkachuk, the incident highlights the strained relationship with some Ottawa supporters after his trade. For BGC Ottawa, the immediate outcome is that the promised collection of jerseys will not arrive in usable condition. Whether Tkachuk follows through with another charitable gesture remains unconfirmed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: John Cena Returning To WWE Raw Next Week—What Will He Announce?
articles.summary: John Cena will make his return to WWE on next week's Raw, and he is expected to make a blockbuster announcement.
articles.body:
John Cena is making his highly anticipated return to WWE programming.

The company revealed on this week's episode of Monday Night Raw that the 17-time world champion will appear on next week's episode of Raw on Netflix, which is the "go-home" show to the Crown Jewel PLE. Following the announcement of Cena's return, the legendary star took to X, formerly Twitter, to tease that he would be making yet another blockbuster announcement on Raw from the Barclays Center in Brooklyn:

After retiring in December 2025, Cena last appeared on WWE programming at Backlash in May, where he made a surprise appearance to announce the creation of "The John Cena Classic." At the time, Cena revealed a few details regarding plans for the event, including:

A format pitting rising NXT stars against established main roster performers

The creation of a "John Cena Classic Championship" belt

Fan voting to determine the champion, so that, in a unique twist, a WWE superstar could lose his or her match and still win the John Cena Classic

Cena himself has repeatedly admitted that he isn't sure how the John Cena Classic will work or if it will work at all. Back in September, he told WrestleRant (h/t Ringside News ), "Even with the John Cena Classic, I'm still swinging big. Like, I'm in the clubhouse, dude. I'm retired. I made it. But I want to put my name on an event that hopefully is a way to to bring people together and and I'm really excited about it and it also might fail."

Although WWE has revealed remarkably few details about the event, a brainchild of Cena himself, there has long been speculation that it will function somewhat similarly to Cena's retirement show. Last December on Saturday Night's Main Event , Cena lost to Gunther in his final match and also used that stage to highlight young up-and-coming talents, including Je'Von Evans, TNA's Leon Slater, Oba Femi and Sol Ruca.

Those stars all benefitted from their presence on that show. Slater is now TNA's World Champion while Evans just challenged for the WWE Championship on this week's Raw. Meanwhile, Ruca would go on to win the Women's Intercontinental Championship, and Femi is already one of the top stars in WWE, with an expected WrestleMania 43 main event possibly on the horizon.

The John Cena Classic had previously been confirmed to take place at some point in December. At one point, WWE was targeting Dec. 12 for the event, but WrestlePalooza will take place on that day instead. The likeliest date for the JCC remains Dec. 19, even though that would put it head-to-head with both AAA and AEW's Worlds End pay-per-view.

With the announcement of Cena's return on next week's Raw, which will be a double taping alongside SmackDown, the expectation is that Cena will reveal the official date and venue for the John Cena Classic as well as perhaps some of the scheduled performers and matches.

That taping also featuring CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens, so WWE is clearly hoping that the addition of Cena's major announcement will result in more buzz and excitement and strong viewership for Raw on Netflix.

articles.title: Best fantasy football waiver wire pickups: 8 players to add for NFL Week 8
articles.summary: With the fantasy football regular season now past the halfway point, it's time to make a playoff push and/or add pieces for a future title run.
articles.body:
The fantasy football regular season has officially passed its midpoint, and by now, you should know whether or not you have a team that can compete for a championship.

That determination has a lot to do with your waiver wire decisions entering Week 8.

If you're on the fringe of contention, you're probably looking for players who can contribute immediately. As usual.

However, if you're in solid position in the standings, this might be a good week to see about possibly stashing players who could be more valuable later than sooner. Someone who could benefit if a higher-profile teammate is traded in the next couple weeks. Or what about a player who's going to be on bye this week and might be overlooked by your win-now leaguemates.

RB Kaelon Black (28% rostered), RB Tyrone Tracy (27%) and WR Malachi Fields (4%) might end up being very useful players after they return next week. (And as always, check out last week's waiver recommendations to see if those players might still be available.)

ON BYE: Houston, New Orleans, N.Y, Giants , San Francisco

NFL Week 7 highlights, standout performances and reactions

Fantasy football players to add for Week 8

Due to the wide variance in types of leagues and individual team needs, the players listed here include their availability in Yahoo leagues , which may or may not match roster rates on other platforms. Suggested bid values based on $100 free agent acquisition budget (FAAB) for the season.

RB Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos (35% rostered)

Coleman is the prime pickup this week, especially in leagues where he couldn't be stashed on injured reserve while he was recovering from an ankle sprain that had kept him out since Week 2. The rookie fourth-round pick led the Broncos with nine carries for 54 yards and caught two passes for 15. Afterward, coach Sean Payton said the team needed to get Coleman more touches. Let's go! ( Recommended FAAB bid: $21)

RB Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts (8% rostered)

Here's another rookie (7th round) who has a chance to make a major impact down the stretch. His snap counts have been gradually increasing, to a season-high 20 in Week 7. He also had his best day as a pro (at Minnesota, even!) with 11 carries for 46 yards on Sunday. But McGowan's real value could come if the Colts decide to trade star RB Jonathan Taylor before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Stash McGowan now while he's cheap. ( FAAB bid: $9)

WR Caleb Douglas, Miami Dolphins (10% rostered)

Like Coleman, Douglas hadn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle sprain. But he showed his big-play ability by catching a pair of touchdown passes from Malik Willis as the Dolphins won their first game of the season. Coincidence? Yeah, probably. But the Dolphins will be forced to throw a lot the rest of the way and Douglas may be their best downfield option. ( FAAB bid: $8)

RB Samaje Perine, Cincinnati Bengals (12% rostered)

Perine continues to deserve a mention, and he may have fallen back into the player pool while the Bengals had their bye week. He didn't do a whole lot in Week 7 with four rushes for 16 yards, but one of those carries was from the 1-yard line. And he punched it in. If the Bengals are going to give Perine the red-zone carries over Chase Brown, he will have value. ( FAAB bid: $7)

The Commanders were off in Week 7, but with the offense struggling to make plays, it's hard to find anyone under-the-radar to add. With top receiver Terry McLaurin out for the season and Stefon Diggs battling injuries, Okonkwo could emerge as an even bigger part of the passing game. With George Kittle, Isaiah Likely and Dalton Schultz all on bye, he makes an interesting dart throw. ( FAAB bid: $3)

TE Mason Taylor, New York Jets (0% rostered)

We've already had Kenyon Sadiq hype week, but Week 3 now seems like a long time ago. And the rookie has caught a total of four passes since then. Taylor is now the man of the hour. He caught a pair of TD passes and added a 2-point conversion for good measure as part of a five-catch, 62-yard day. After missing Weeks 3 and 4 with a thumb injury, Taylor has 12 receptions in the last three games. ( FAAB bid: $2)

QB Geno Smith, New York Jets (18% rostered)

Someone had to get Taylor the ball this past week, and Smith did a nice job of it. He completed 23-of-30 passes for 287 yards and three TDs, with the other score going to rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. If the Jets get RB Breece Hall back into the mix this week, it could be another solid week for Smith in a "revenge game" at home against his former team, the Raiders . One last bye-week stash: The Texans are having trouble running the ball. And they have a wealth of options in the passing game. Maybe this past week was an anomaly; certainly Nico Collins needs to have more than two catches for 6 yards. But the team leader in targets (6) and receptions (3) against the Giants wasn't Collins or Marvin Harrison Jr. or Jaylin Noel or even Tank Dell. It was Hutchinson, who also caught a touchdown pass. articles.title: Ballon d'Or in London - the most chaotic ever?
articles.summary: It was the first time the Ballon d'Or had been held in London in its 70-year history - but the event was not plain sailing. BBC Sport assesses a chaotic nigh...
articles.body:
It was the first time the Ballon d'Or had been held in London in its 70-year history, with organisers choosing the iconic London Palladium as the venue.

Despite the perfect homecoming for Harry Kane on Monday night, the rest of the event was not plain sailing.

Did the organisers give away the winners early or was it just a simple mix-up? Why was the ceremony delayed and why was the audience booing?

BBC Sport assesses a chaotic night in central London.

London traffic can cause issues on any day but unfortunately for the Ballon d'Or organisers, they chose to hold a major event just a stone's throw from Oxford Street on the same day the famous shopping area was made traffic-free.

That, coupled with large crowds at the event entrance, meant significant numbers of guests were delayed and the start had to be pushed back by 45 minutes.

Once it did get under way, a rowdy and boisterous audience sat through a ceremony that lasted nearly two and a half hours. On a number of occasions, hosts Kate Scott and Thierry Henry had to briefly pause proceedings while people shouted the names of players in the audience and there were several instances of booing during commercial breaks.

After Kane and Alexia Putellas had been crowned the winners in the two main categories, they then spoke to the world's media in separate press conferences.

Journalists were able to put questions to Putellas but only men were selected to ask Kane a question, with several female journalists having their attempts seemingly ignored.

The Ballon d'Or team has since apologised.

Hundreds of people gathered outside the London Palladium to try to get a glimpse of the biggest stars in football on the red carpet. A security perimeter of metal fencing and barricades had been erected to try to keep those without a ticket out.

But the BBC Sport team witnessed those barriers being scaled, broken and ripped down and several people being evicted by security after making their way through.

The atmosphere at times was tense, with footage on social media appearing to show fans clashing with security and police.

The BBC has approached the Metropolitan Police for comment.

The confusion and chaos began hours before the ceremony had even started, after the official Ballon d'Or website published an article declaring Kane as the winner of the men's award.

Further digging revealed similar articles had been published about some of the other favourites to win the men's and women's awards, including Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and London City Lionesses' Putellas.

Was it a genuine mistake? Or a case of trying to divert people's attention from the initial Kane announcement? Which of course turned out to be true.

A Ballon d'Or spokesperson told BBC Sport last night they were "inadvertently published online".

"These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings," the spokesperson said.

articles.title: Why Carrick Had To Drop Manchester United Captain Bruno Fernandes
articles.summary: Why Michael Carrick had to drop Bruno Fernandes, what recent dressing-room disputes reveal, and whether a harder line can turn Manchester United’s troubled s...
articles.body:
Michael Carrick was left with no choice. Whether he'd made the decision in the immediate aftermath of Bruno Fernandes's public criticism of his tactics in Como last week or shortly before last weekend's defeat to Bournemouth, the Manchester United head coach had to act.

His captain had left him with no choice. For Carrick to retain any level of credibility within the Old Trafford dressing room – or, in fact, show he won't tolerate such insubordination in a future role – he had to leave the Portuguese out of his next team.

Carrick claimed Fernandes was dropped for "purely sporting reasons" when quizzed about the decision following the 3-0 loss against Bournemouth, although it's easy to assume there was more to it. To leave out an ever-present skipper and his side's best player only days after giving the interview Fernandes did is a mighty coincidence otherwise.

But while the beleaguered coach's show of strength didn't reap immediate rewards, if there is any hope of a reprieve in the coming weeks, he needs to take a hard-line approach.

It's a common move made by bosses trying to get hold of a difficult dressing room, either at a point of crisis or upon their arrival. It's a jolt to the team that shows every player, regardless of talent or status, has to buy into the expected discipline of the club – and that extends to publicly sounding off about the manager.

In Carrick's playing days, he wouldn't have dared speak out against legendary United boss Alex Ferguson and while Fergie's iron-fist approach may not have had quite the same effect in the modern game, the theory remains sound. The man in charge can't be willingly undermined.

Another of Carrick's predecessors, Erik ten Hag, wasn't averse to doing the same when it was needed. He left out Cristiano Ronaldo after the forward refused to come on as a substitute against Spurs – a rift that ended with Ronaldo leaving the club – and named Marcus Rashford on the bench after the Englishman missed a team meeting.

It's not just a United thing, either. Only last season, Chelsea imposed a two-game internal suspension on Enzo Fernandez after the Argentinian made public overtures towards Real Madrid, while Mo Salah was left out of the Liverpool squad when he spoke about being "thrown under the bus" and his failing relationship with boss Arne Slot.

A key moment in Mikel Arteta's early reign at Arsenal also came when he stripped Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang of the captaincy for not returning home on time from a club-approved visit to France in 2021.

Some of these incidents end more successfully than others. But while there are many more factors at play for a coach, history suggests that maintaining strong standards and values is always a strong basis to work from.

For Carrick, the question is if he turns to Fernandes again for this weekend's match with Chelsea, which the United boss is expected to remain in charge of despite rumours about his job security.

Since the Bournemouth defeat, the Red Devils captain has been noted for liking an Instagram post about "loyal people getting taken for granted". What goes on behind the scenes will likely dictate what happens next, but taking Fernandes out of the firing line for only one game may not be deemed more than a token effort.

Instead, there's a fair chance that Carrick names Fernandes on the bench at Stamford Bridge again and expects him to earn his place back in the side from there. It shouldn't be too difficult given United's abject run of form.

Although if Carrick can stumble upon an effective way of playing without his talisman in the team, creating a more balanced midfield that doesn't play almost entirely through the playmaker, there's no guarantee how this ends.

The trouble for Carrick and Manchester United as a whole is that, with Fernandes in the team or not, the trajectory is unequivocally downwards.

articles.title: Where Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. ranks statistically after Week 7
articles.summary: Where Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. ranks statistically after Week 7
articles.body:
The radical improvement of Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix was on full display this past week. Penix put in his best game yet this season against San Francisco, getting the ball out quickly and accurately. In the end he completed 25 of 34 pass attempts for 213 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions.

That puts Penix at 1,157 yards, nine touchdowns and just one pick on the season. Let's see where those numbers rank Penix statistically going into Week 8.

By now we have established that Penix has leveled his game up. Now the only question is if he can do so consistently.

Next up Penix will face a Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense that ranks 14th against the pass. Only five teams are giving up fewer fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this year.

articles.title: Urban Meyer blasts Michigan's offensive playcalling under Jason Beck
articles.summary: Urban Meyer and Mark Ingram criticize Michigan football's offensive play calling and lack of quarterback freedom.
articles.body:
The Fox Big Noon Kickoff crew was in Ann Arbor this past week, and they did not like what they saw from Michigan football.

Yes, the Wolverines held Indiana close, taking the defending national champion to overtime after holding IU to just six points in regulation. But the offense is completely dysfunctional. And no matter how much hand-waving that the Michigan staff might make, the struggles cannot be unseen.

On the Triple Option Podcast, former Alabama running back Mark Ingram simply noted the disparity between the elite defense and not just the offense, but the calls that the offensive coordinator, Jason Beck, made in the game.

"The offensive play calls are crazy. There's no like purpose behind them," Ingram said. "It's just, it's very stagnant on the other side of the ball. But their defense is one of the best in the country."

Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer, who oversaw Kyle Whittingham during his tenure at Utah, spoke more on Beck. He noted that it simply just isn't a personnel issue or even an execution one. As far as he can tell, whether it's Tommy Carr or Bryce Underwood, they don't have the freedom to get out of a bad play call, and Beck seems to call quite a few of them.

"I know him a little bit. I met him a few times, and he did good at New Mexico and at Utah, but it just doesn't look good," Meyer said. "They're running plays that, like -- to me, offensive football is numbers and leverage, period. Numbers and leverage. When you have a five and a nine or outside leverage techniques, and you run a jet sweep for minus five yards, the quarterback's got to get you out of that play. And I was talking to Brady -- Brady Quinn, he doesn't think he does. Those are, once again, questions for the Wolverines to figure out.

"But when I see bad plays that you can blame that tailback or their handoff or even the offensive line on that -- that was a minus five on a jet sweep run into out-leveraged defense. Why? That's one of those, like, whoa, whoa, whoa. From the sideline, if I saw that and our quarterback didn't get it, I'm screaming timeout because it's second-and-15. I don't care what you do. It's second-and-15. So when I see stuff like that, you're like, no, that's not Bryce Underwood, or that's not Tommy Carr. It's not the tailback."

Meyer continued, firmly establishing that there were multiple plays called in the game that simply should have never been called. And the players aren't empowered to change course when it's obvious to everyone that something must give on any given down.

"If a quarterback does not have access to get you out of a bad play, that's to me, that's like I'm scratching my head right now," Meyer said. "Several times in that game, they should have never ran that play."

Multiple times against Indiana, Michigan found itself driving, only to give up a negative play -- particularly sacks -- on pivotal third downs. And that included two third-and-goals with the ball on the one and the three.
